# How to run an example

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/reproducing/

Choose the right Leafony hardware, development tool, and source files, then check the build, upload, and execution results in order.

Match the **leaf configuration and development tool, then check the build → upload → execution result in order**. This makes it easier to find where a problem starts. Choose a purpose or CPU from the [example catalog](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/) and check the required items in the article.

## 1. Match your hardware

- Check the **processor model number**. Even examples using the same temperature and humidity sensor need different board selections and upload procedures for AVR, STM32, and ESP32.
- Gather the **leaves and additional parts**. Check the model numbers, power supply, antenna, SIM, and other requirements in the article, as well as the kit name. Turn off the power before assembling, attaching, or removing leaves.
- Choose the **development tool**. Open Arduino IDE sketches, PlatformIO projects, and STM32CubeIDE projects using their respective procedures. Start with your CPU under [Development environment](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/).

## 2. Obtain the source and libraries

Use the article's source link to obtain all files required by the example. A sample with multiple files needs its headers and configuration files as well as the main `.ino` or `main.cpp`.

| Development tool | What to open and check |
| --- | --- |
| Arduino IDE | The sketch folder and `.ino` file. Install the libraries and board package specified in the article |
| PlatformIO | The project folder containing `platformio.ini`. Check `board`, `lib_deps`, and the upload destination |
| STM32CubeIDE | The project folder containing `.project` and `.cproject`. Obtain `Core`, `Drivers`, and the other project files together |

GitHub links to `main` or `master` can change as the source is updated. Use a complete set from the same revision instead of mixing old and new files. Keep a copy of a previously working project before updating it so you can compare the changes.

Libraries with similar names may be different implementations. Use the source specified in the article and check its CPU and Arduino Core requirements. For STM32, for example, see [RTC and low-power library compatibility with the Core](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/#library-versions-in-older-samples).

## 3. Check three stages

| Stage | Success check | If it stops here |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | Compilation completes without errors | Read the first error and check the board, CPU, and required libraries |
| Upload | The development tool reports a successful upload | Check the USB cable, port, power supply, and program switch |
| Execution | You obtain the LED pattern, serial output, received data, or other result described in the article | Check the switch to run mode, reset, wiring, and communication destination |

**A successful build or upload is a separate check from successful operation.** For communication examples, check the receiver or saved data as well as the transmitter log. Sensor values depend on the surroundings: check that readings are obtained and respond to changes, rather than expecting the same numbers as the screenshot.

## 4. If it does not work

Start with the article's troubleshooting section and the [FAQ](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/). When contacting support, include the leaves, development tool, sample URL, stage reached, and first error. Do not send passwords, tokens, or SIM identifiers.

In the catalog, **Upcoming examples** are not yet published. **Previous versions & reference** may use different procedures or conditions from current examples. Read any notices about discontinued external services before using them.

---

# Help and questions

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/

Search answers about identifying leaves, power, uploads, connections and using Leafony. Open the question form if you cannot find an answer.

This page covers first-time questions such as “Which leaf do I have?” as well as checks when something does not work. Start with the item that matches your question. For programming and development tools, use the [MCU setup instructions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) and [library list](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/libraries/) to check settings for your model and tool.

**Identifying leaves**

- [Where can I find my leaf's model number?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#where-can-i-find-my-leafs-model-number)
- [Do I need to check the letter at the end of the model number?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#do-i-need-to-check-the-letter-at-the-end-of-the-model-number)
- [Cannot find or read the model number](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#cannot-find-or-read-the-model-number)

**Power and assembly**

- [Power will not turn on](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#power-will-not-turn-on)

**Computer connections and uploads**

- [Serial port is missing](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#serial-port-is-missing)
- [Upload fails](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#upload-fails)

**Display and wireless connections**

- [No text appears on the LCD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#no-text-appears-on-the-lcd)
- [BLE will not connect or no device is found](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#ble-will-not-connect-or-no-device-is-found)

- [ESP32 Wi-Fi cannot connect or the demo page will not open](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#esp32-wifi)
- [How do I restore the kit demo?](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#restore-demo)

## Where can I find my leaf's model number?

**Look for the model number (part number) printed on the board. Start with the back.** Many leaves have a code such as `AZ01C` or `AI04A` printed on the back. The position varies by leaf, so check the front too if you cannot find it.

1. **Look for text on the board itself.** Black components may also have text on them, but those markings identify the components. The leaf's model number is printed directly on the board.
2. **Read the complete model number.** For example, if it says `AZ01C`, include the final `C` when you write it down.
3. **Open the matching documentation from the [leaf reference](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/).** Compare the model number, front and back photos, and features such as the USB connector or display with the leaf you have.

  Example: the back of the USB-C leaf. AZ01C is its model number. Select the photo to enlarge it.

| Example marking on the board | What the leaf does | Documentation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AZ01C` | Connects to a computer via USB-C | [AZ01C USB-C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/) |
| `AI04A` | Displays text and numbers | [AI04 LCD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04/) |
| `AP01A` | Runs a program | [AP01 AVR MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap01/) |

Before separating stacked leaves to check the markings, unplug the USB cable and disconnect batteries and any other power sources.

## Do I need to check the letter at the end of the model number?

**Yes. Check the complete printed model number when choosing instructions.**

A page title may use a shorter name such as `AP01` or `AI04`, while the board is marked `AP01A`, `AP01B` or `AI04A`. Different suffixes may indicate differences in board specifications or operating procedures. For example, [AZ01 USB](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01/) and [AZ01C USB-C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/) have different USB connectors and reset procedures when uploading to AP01.

After opening the documentation, check that the instructions apply to the model you have.

## Cannot find or read the model number

Try taking photos of both sides of the board with your smartphone and zooming in. If the markings are hidden in a stack, you can also compare the leaves listed on your kit's [product page](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/) with the photos in the [leaf reference](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/).

To narrow down the candidates, compare **readable markings, connector type, and the positions of switches and components** with front and back photos in the documentation. For example, a USB-C connector suggests [AZ01C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/), a text display suggests [AI04](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04/), and a CR2032 holder suggests [AV01](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av01/). Compare the whole board and suffix rather than deciding from one feature alone. Disconnect all power before separating leaves to take photos.

## Power will not turn on

**Check the battery, the power switch, and the contact between leaves, in that order.** Go through the items below from the top.

- Is there enough remaining battery power?
- Is the button battery inserted in the correct direction?
- Is the power switch turned on?
- Are the connectors clean? If they are dirty, wipe them lightly with a paper wiper moistened with anhydrous ethanol. If the problem persists, replace the connectors. For the steps, see [Installing and removing connectors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az61/#installing-and-removing-connectors).
- Are the screws tight enough? If they are loose, tighten them alternately.

  [](https://docs.leafony.com/faq/assembly.png)

## Serial port is missing

**First check that your USB cable supports data transfer, then check the driver for your USB leaf.**

- Use a USB cable that supports data transfer. A two-wire power-only USB cable cannot carry data.
- Check that the driver required by your USB leaf is installed. See these resources for FTDI USB serial converter drivers:
  - [VCP Drivers](https://ftdichip.com/drivers/vcp-drivers/)
  - [Installation Guides](https://ftdichip.com/document/installation-guides/)
  - [Manually installing an FTDI USB serial driver on Windows (Japanese)](https://www.monoxit.com/tecmat/windowsftdiusb/)

## Upload fails

Read the complete IDE error message, then open the instructions for your microcontroller and USB leaf.

- **AP01 / AP01B (AVR MCU) + AZ01C (USB-C)**: Follow the [AZ01C upload instructions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/#uploading-to-ap01-avr-mcu) to check the board and port settings and the manual reset procedure.
- **Other configurations**: Use [development environment setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) to select the instructions for AP01 (AVR), AP02 (ESP32) or AP03 (STM32) and your development tools.

## No text appears on the LCD

For AI04, check **LCD power, initialization, and contrast**, in that order.

1. Choose the LCD example for your MCU from the [example catalog](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/). The published examples use tomozh’s `arduino_ST7032` library.
2. Enable LCD power through the I2C I/O Expander. Calling `lcd.begin()` alone does not control the leaf’s power switch.
3. Initialize the LCD in the sample’s order, set the contrast, and display text.

See [AI04 power and initialization](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04/#powering-and-initializing-the-lcd) for the operations and addresses. If `ST7032.h` is missing, see the [library error checklist](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/library-not-found/).

## BLE will not connect or no device is found

Use the guide that matches your kit and the program currently installed on it to check supported devices, browsers and connection methods.

- **The preinstalled AVR MCU demo in Basic Kit or Basic Kit 2**: Follow the [Basic Kit getting started guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic/) for your Android device, computer, iPhone or iPad.
- **The preinstalled STM32 MCU demo in Basic Kit 2**: See the [Basic Kit 2 getting started guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/) for beacon reception, connections and browser requirements.
- **After uploading an example or your own program**: Open the relevant article in the [example catalog](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/) and check that program's instructions, including its device name and receiving application. Its behavior may differ from the preinstalled demos above.

Once a device is found, use its symptoms to narrow down the cause:

- **Discovered, but unable to connect:** STM32 Simple BLE Beacon is configured not to accept connections. See [beacons versus connection-based samples](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ble-beacon-connection/).
- **Connected, but unable to read values:** Compare UUIDs, notification settings, and data formats in the transmitter and receiver. [BLE data formats and receiver code](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ble-data-format/) lists what to check.

## ESP32 Wi-Fi cannot connect or the demo page will not open

This checklist is for the preinstalled touch-sensor demo in ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit / Kit 2. Work from the first stage that fails.

| Stage | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| `Leafony_ESP32-AP` does not appear | Power, battery orientation and charge, and whether the MCU still contains the demo. Another sketch will not necessarily create this network. |
| The network appears but connection fails | Select `Leafony_ESP32-AP` and enter `password` as shown in the [getting started guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/esp32/). Use the new credentials if you changed the sketch. |
| Connected, but the page does not open | Confirm that the device is still connected to Leafony's Wi-Fi. Enter `http://192.168.4.1` in the address bar, including `http://`. This demo serves a local page and does not require an internet connection. If asked whether to stay on a network without internet, keep the Leafony connection. |
| The page opens but readings do not change | Touch pin 26 as shown in the guide. If automatic updates are stopped, select `1 second` or reload the page. Check the pin assignment before touching other pins. |

If you changed the program, use the SSID and address configured by that program. To test with the preinstalled demo’s instructions, follow [the demo restoration steps](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#restore-demo) and select the program for your MCU.

## How do I restore the kit demo?

Resetting or cycling power restarts the uploaded program; it does not restore the preinstalled sketch. Select the demo for the MCU you have, then upload its source again.

| MCU / kit | Demo to upload | Where to check the result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| AP01 AVR in Basic Kit / Basic Kit 2 | [Web Bluetooth IoT example](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/basic/webbluetooth_iot/), using the `4-Sensors_BLE` source linked there | [Basic Kit guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic/): connect to `Leafony_AC02` and view readings |
| AP03 STM32 in Basic Kit 2 | [STM32 Logger Beacon](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/stm32_logger_ble_beacon/) | [Basic Kit 2 guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/): connect, record, then read data |
| AP02 ESP32 in ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit / Kit 2 | [Wi-Fi touch sensor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/esp32-mcu/esp32/wifi_touchsensor/) | [ESP32 guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/esp32/): join `Leafony_ESP32-AP` and view touch readings |

Before uploading, check the example's required leaves and libraries and follow [setup for your MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/). Save any source code you want to keep. Re-uploading a demo does not necessarily reset settings or erase stored measurements; follow that demo's instructions for those operations.

## Still need help?

First, search the [public Q&A](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/) for the error message, leaf model, or communication technology. These resources also provide specific checks.

| Problem | Where to look next |
| --- | --- |
| Building or uploading | [Development environment](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) and [library list](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/libraries/) |
| Adding a leaf or sensor | [Combining leaves and choosing power](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/) |
| Running a sample | [Running examples](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/reproducing/) |

For individual conditions not covered by the documentation, the [question form](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ask/) lets you describe the steps and results you checked. If an order or fault requires action, use the [Leafony Shop contact page (Japanese)](https://shop.leafony.com/pages/contact-us).

# Assembling and Replacing Leaves

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/assembly/

Check power before stacking leaves, attach ACR connectors, use spacers, secure the stack with screws and a Nut Plate, and test your new configuration.

Use these common steps when adding a leaf or replacing an MCU. **Follow the leaf selection and stacking order in the kit or example you are using.** Before changing the functional configuration, read [Combining Leaves and Choosing a Power Supply](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/) to check power and pin requirements.

## What You Need

| Part or document | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Leaves to use | Model, revision, front/back orientation, and whether they match the example |
| [AZ61 Connector](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az61/) | ACR (anisotropic conductive rubber) connectors between leaves |
| [AZ62 Connector Cover](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az62/) | Protects exposed connectors from dirt |
| Screws and [AZ63 Nut Plate](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az63/) | Fasteners of the length and quantity specified for the configuration |
| [AX04 Spacer](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax04/) | Used where the example specifies one or where adjacent components interfere |
| Kit or example assembly diagram | Stacking order and battery, USB, and external device connections |

If you do not know a leaf's model, see [How to Identify Your Leaves](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/). Screw length and spacer requirements depend on the stack, so another kit's fastening parts may not be suitable.

## 1. Disconnect All Power

Turn the power switch OFF and disconnect USB cables, batteries, and power from external circuits. Even with a power leaf's switch OFF, check that no other source, such as USB, remains connected before removing the screws.

Take a photo of the existing stacking order so that you can restore it later.

## 2. Check Connectors and Orientation

An ACR connector electrically connects the contacts when compressed between leaves. If a connector is detached, check the white line and attachment direction shown below.

For removal, see the [AZ61 attachment and removal diagrams](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az61/). If a connector is dirty, check it using the [power troubleshooting steps](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/) before stacking the leaves.

## 3. Follow the Assembly Diagram

Align the bus contacts and screw holes, and follow the front/back orientation and order in the kit or example diagram. If components touch another leaf or a board sits at an angle, do not force it into place with the screws. Review the configuration first.

Use an AX04 Spacer to increase clearance between components. Check the leaf or example documentation for the required position.

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax04/ax04a_p_large.jpg)

For a specific example, see [Replacing AVR with STM32 in Basic Kit 2](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/). The screws and stacking order in that example are for Basic Kit 2.

## 4. Secure the Stack Before Applying Power

Use the specified screws and Nut Plate. Tighten the screws alternately, checking for looseness or uneven alignment. **Use AZ63 Nut Plate: ordinary hex nuts may touch the board contacts and cause a short circuit.**

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/others/az63/az63a_large.jpg)

Before applying power, check the following:

- Bus contacts and screw holes align, and components do not touch each other.
- Connectors are in their correct positions and the screws are secure.
- Battery type and polarity match the power leaf's input requirements.
- The program switch is in the correct position for running or uploading the program.
- If using USB and a battery together, the power conditions for each leaf have been checked.

After completing these checks, connect the power source specified by the kit or example.

## 5. Test a Simple Function First

After replacement, use the development environment and program for the selected MCU. Start with a basic example, such as printing sensor readings to the serial monitor, to check connections and software in stages.

| Symptom | What to check next |
| --- | --- |
| No power | [Power, connector, and screw checks](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/) |
| Upload fails | [Upload troubleshooting](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#upload-fails) |
| Communication stops after adding a leaf | [Configuration checks](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/) and the [I2C Address Map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/) |
| Unsure which program to use | [Development Environment](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) and [Examples](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/) |

---

# Basic Kit / Basic Kit 2: Your First AVR Demo

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic/

Use the preinstalled AVR demo to view temperature, humidity, illuminance and acceleration over BLE. These first steps are shared by Basic Kit and Basic Kit 2 and need no development tools.

**If your Basic Kit 2 has just arrived, start here too.** Its preinstalled AVR demo is shared with Basic Kit. Keep the kit assembled with its AVR MCU; you do not need to swap the processor.

Use the program preinstalled on the AVR MCU to view temperature, humidity, illuminance and acceleration readings over BLE on a phone or computer. **You do not need to upload a program or install development tools.** The separate STM32 MCU included in Basic Kit 2 is not used for this first check.

## What to prepare

- Basic Kit or Basic Kit 2 with its AVR MCU installed
- A CR2032 coin cell battery
- A phone or computer with Bluetooth LE and a supported browser

| Device | Browser to use |
| --- | --- |
| Android, macOS or Windows | Google Chrome with Web Bluetooth support |
| iPhone or iPad | [Bluefy](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bluefy-web-ble-browser/id1492822055) |
| Linux | Chrome requires additional setup; see the instructions below |

The [Web Bluetooth implementation status](https://github.com/WebBluetoothCG/web-bluetooth/blob/main/implementation-status.md) describes browser support. OS and browser support alone do not guarantee that this demo works on every device. Start by checking the on-screen readings.

## Setup

Insert the CR2032 coin cell in the orientation shown, then turn the power switch ON.

## Usage

### For Android, macOS or Windows

1. Enable Bluetooth on your device and open Google Chrome.
2. Open the [Leafony Web Bluetooth app](https://docs.leafony.com/WebBluetooth_for_Leafony_app/).
3. Press **Leafonyに接続する** (Connect to Leafony). Select **Leafony_AC02** in your device's pairing dialog and pair. Allow Bluetooth access if prompted.
4. Check that temperature, humidity and other readings appear and the Leafony LED blinks.

This is an example of the previous interface. In the current app, use **Leafonyに接続する** (Connect to Leafony).

### For iPhone or iPad

1. Install and open [Bluefy](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bluefy-web-ble-browser/id1492822055).
2. Enable Bluetooth and allow Bluefy to access it if prompted.
3. Open `https://docs.leafony.com/WebBluetooth_for_Leafony_app/` in Bluefy.
4. Press **Leafonyに接続する** (Connect to Leafony), select **Leafony_AC02** in your device's pairing dialog, and pair. Check the readings on screen and the blinking LED.

### On Linux

The official compatibility table lists Linux as partially implemented and unsupported. Check the [Linux notes and required settings](https://github.com/WebBluetoothCG/web-bluetooth/blob/main/implementation-status.md) first, then follow the Chrome connection steps above. If setup is difficult, use another device from the table for the initial demo.

## Check that it worked

**When sensor readings appear in the web app and the Leafony LED blinks, your first check is complete.** CSV export and changing the program are not needed for this check.

Open **LEDの調整・データの保存** (LED settings and data export) to change the LED blink speed or export readings. Adjust the LED while connected, and use **CSVを保存する** (Save CSV) to export received readings. When finished, select **接続を切る** (Disconnect).

## Troubleshooting

If the device does not appear, see [BLE connection checks](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#ble-will-not-connect-or-no-device-is-found). If you uploaded a different program, follow [Restore the demo](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#restore-demo); restarting the MCU does not restore it.

## Next steps

- **Upload your first program with AVR (AP01)**: [Set up Arduino IDE and check the blinking LED](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/avr/arduino/). The first Blink example needs no additional libraries.
- **Understand the AVR demo**: [Web Bluetooth IoT example and source code](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/basic/webbluetooth_iot/)
- **When you need more memory or processing capacity (optional)**: Swap in the STM32 (AP03) included in Basic Kit 2 and [try its preinstalled demo](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/). You can also continue developing with AVR.

For a different MCU or development tool, use the [development environment list](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/). Uploading a program replaces the current demo, so check how to restore it before continuing.

## Leaves included in the kit

**For Basic Kit 2, see its [included leaves](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/basic2/#contents).** The AVR demo on this page is shared, but the kit contents differ.

  Show the contents of the original Basic Kit

# Basic Kit 2: Try STM32 Logging and BLE

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/

An optional guide to sensor logging and BLE after swapping in the STM32 MCU included in Basic Kit 2. Start with the assembled AVR demo when your kit arrives.

**This guide is for trying the demo after swapping in the included STM32 MCU.** When your Basic Kit 2 arrives, start with the [assembled AVR demo](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic/). You can keep using AVR; switching to STM32 is optional.

Basic Kit 2 lets you display sensor readings on a phone or computer. Both the AVR and STM32 MCUs have a demo sketch installed, so **you can try the original demos without uploading a program or setting up a development environment.**

## Try the preinstalled demos

1. **If this is your first time, start with the AVR demo.** Keep the kit assembled and follow the [AVR demo shared by Basic Kit and Basic Kit 2](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic/).
2. **Consider STM32 when you need more memory or processing capacity.** If you choose to swap the MCU, use this page to try on-device logging and low-power operation.

The rest of this page covers the STM32 demo. If you have already uploaded a different sketch, see the [STM32 Logger Beacon sample](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/stm32_logger_ble_beacon/) for instructions on uploading the original demo.

## Required items and browser support

- Basic Kit 2 and its CR2032 coin cell
- A Bluetooth-capable phone or computer
- Google Chrome on a supported system such as Android, Windows or Mac; [Bluefy](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bluefy-web-ble-browser/id1492822055) on iPhone or iPad

For the first check, connect to retrieve the log and view the graph on screen. Receiving beacons is optional. See [Browser compatibility](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/#browser-compatibility) later on this page for the detailed requirements.

## Setup

Before changing the stack, check the [assembly and leaf replacement basics](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/assembly/).

1. Turn the power off and disconnect USB before changing the leaves. Remove the [Connector Cover](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az62/) from the STM32 MCU. Remove the AVR MCU and USB leaf from the assembled block, then install the STM32 MCU as shown.

2. Set the STM32 MCU's program switch to **Run**.

3. Insert the CR2032 coin cell and turn the power switch on.

## View sensor readings

### Connect and start logging

1. Turn Bluetooth on and open the [STM32 Logger Beacon web app](https://docs.leafony.com/Sample-Sketches/STM32_Logger_Beacon/sample_web_app/lescan/) in a supported browser. Allow Bluetooth access if requested.
2. Shake Leafony to enter its connection window, then select **Connect** in the web app within about 20 seconds. Select **Leaf_A** (the initial device name) from the list and pair. The connection sets the device's clock automatically. Continue when the app shows **Connected**.
3. **Check the measurement interval while still connected.** Select **Check interval** in step 2 of the app and note the number of seconds shown. You can try the current setting first.
4. Select **Disconnect to start recording**. Leave Leafony powered on and wait at least the interval you noted before retrieving the log below.

If the device does not appear in the list, shake it and try selecting it again. It waits for a connection for about 20 seconds. To change the interval, open **Interval, name and stored data** while connected, enter the number of seconds, and select **Save interval**.

### Retrieve the log and view the graph

1. Shake the device and reconnect using **Connect** in step 1 of the web app.
2. Select **Read stored data (Get Data)** in step 4 of the app. After the stored data is received, graphs show temperature, humidity, illuminance and battery voltage.
3. The app disconnects automatically when the transfer finishes. Connect again when you want to retrieve newer readings.

If the graphs do not show any readings yet, use **Check interval** while connected, select **Disconnect to start recording**, wait, and retrieve the log again.

## Check that it worked

**When measurement times and values appear in the graphs, your connection, recording and retrieval check is complete.** Try beacon reception or CSV download after checking your browser's support.

## Next steps

After trying the demo, set up a development environment when you want to upload your own programs.

- **Upload your first program with STM32 (AP03)**: [Set up Arduino IDE and display temperature and humidity](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/arduino_ide/), or [write a Hello World program with PlatformIO](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/)
- **Understand the STM32 demo**: [How STM32 Logger Beacon works and its source code](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/stm32_logger_ble_beacon/)
- **Change the AVR (AP01) program**: [Set up Arduino IDE for AVR and check the blinking LED](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/avr/arduino/)

For a different STM32 development tool, see the [STM32 development environment](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/).

## Restore the demo

If you uploaded a different program, use the [MCU-specific demo restoration guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#restore-demo). Basic Kit 2 has separate AVR and STM32 demos; select the one for the MCU currently in the stack.

## Leaves included in the kit

## How the STM32 demo works

The STM32 demo normally measures, stores readings and broadcasts beacons, sleeping between cycles to reduce battery use. Connect to a PC or phone when you need to set the clock or measurement interval, or retrieve the stored log.

You can retrieve the readings stored in the device in a batch. Check the browser notes below for connecting or receiving beacons.

## Web Bluetooth

The web app can retrieve and graph up to 169 samples stored in the device. If this is your first time, follow [View sensor readings](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/#view-sensor-readings) on this page to connect, record measurements and retrieve the log.

### Browser compatibility

- **Connecting to read the log** and **receiving beacons without a connection** have different browser requirements. Chrome provides the connection feature on Android, Windows, Mac and other supported systems. The official compatibility table lists Linux as partially implemented and unsupported, requiring additional settings.
- **Receiving beacons is optional.** The web app describes this feature for Android. Chrome's Scanning API is experimental and requires `chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features` on a supported system. See the [Web Bluetooth implementation status](https://github.com/WebBluetoothCG/web-bluetooth/blob/main/implementation-status.md) for details.
- **On iPhone and iPad, open the web app in Bluefy.** Use the on-screen graph for your first check.

## Demo video

## Measurement interval and battery life

The measurement interval depends on the installed sketch and saved settings. The original guide estimates that intervals of several minutes may allow months of CR2032 coin cell operation. This is a theoretical estimate, not a measured runtime guarantee; battery condition, supply losses and the program's activity affect runtime. See [low-power design](https://docs.leafony.com/en/lowpower/) for the calculation method.

# Cat-M1 Kit Start Guide

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/cellular-lpwa-cat-m1/

Send temperature and humidity directly to the cloud with the compact, low-power Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 Kit. Check the contents, assemble the kit, upload the sample, and record data in Google Sheets.

[Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 Kit](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/cellular-lpwa-cat-m1/) is a **compact, low-power development kit that sends sensor data directly to the cloud over a cellular network**. You can record temperature and humidity in remote locations without setting up Wi-Fi.

## 1. Kit contents

The leaves arrive individually packed in bags. First, check that you have all the following leaves and accessories.

  Assembly example and accessories. The leaves arrive individually packed in bags.

### Leaves

### Accessories

## 2. What you will build

The goal of this guide is to run the sample program and **record the temperature and humidity measured by the kit in Google Sheets every 10 minutes**.

The data follows this path:

```text
Measure temperature and humidity with AI05 → Send over a cellular network with AC09 → Record in Google Sheets
```

Each row in the spreadsheet contains the reception timestamp, temperature, and humidity. You can also chart the recorded data to see how the values change over time.

## 3. What you need

Prepare the following items in addition to the kit.

| Item | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| Computer with internet access | Install the development tools, upload the program, and set up the spreadsheet. |
| USB-C cable that supports data transfer | Connect the computer to the included AZ01C USB-C leaf. A charging-only cable will not work. |
| Two AA batteries | Put these in the included battery holder when you try battery power at the end of the guide. |
| Screwdriver that fits the screws | Tighten the screws that secure the leaves. |
| Google account | Create the Google spreadsheet that will store the data. |

Complete these preparations on your computer:

1. Follow [Development environment setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/) to install **VS Code, PlatformIO, and STM32CubeProgrammer**.
2. Check that the included **1NCE SIM is ready to use** and confirm its assigned **APN (the setting for connecting to the cellular network)**. Refer to the kit's sales information for activation instructions.
3. Follow [Prepare Google Sheets](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/ac09_google_sheets/#prepare-google-sheets) to set up the destination spreadsheet and the Apps Script that receives data. Note the issued **endpoint URL** and the **authentication token** you configured.

## 4. Assemble the kit

**Disconnect the USB cable and batteries before assembly.**

Watch the assembly from SIM installation (Japanese)

1. Prepare the included 1NCE SIM in nanoSIM size and insert it into the AC09 SIM holder. Check the card's notch and the shape of the holder.
2. Align the bus contacts and screw holes, then stack the leaves in the order shown below.
3. Check the connector orientation and make sure components do not touch each other, then secure the stack with the included **M2×18 mm screws** and **AZ63 Nut Plate**.

The assembled stack must have the following order **from top to bottom**:

| Position | Leaf |
| --- | --- |
| 1 (top) | [AI05 Env Sensors leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/) |
| 2 | [AZ01C USB-C leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/) |
| 3 | [AP03B STM32 leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03b/) |
| 4 | [AX04 Spacer leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax04/) |
| 5 | [AC09 Cat-M1 leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/) |
| 6 (bottom) | [AV06 power leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av06/) |

Place the **Spacer leaf between the STM32 and Cat-M1 leaves**. The included [AX02B 29-pin leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax02b/) is for connecting external circuits, so leave it out of this stack.

See [Assembly and reconfiguration basics](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/assembly/) for guidance on stacking leaves and tightening the screws.

## 5. Upload the sample code

### Open and configure the sample

1. Obtain the sample from the [AC09 development repository](https://github.com/leafony/ac09-cat-m1-ty) and open the **`platformio/google_sheets` folder** in VS Code. If you cannot access the repository, see [Obtain the source](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/ac09_google_sheets/#obtain-the-source).
2. Copy `include/config.example.h` to **`config.local.h`** in the same folder.
3. Update the following entries in `config.local.h` with your settings.

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `GAS_URL` | The Apps Script URL you prepared. Use the URL ending in `/exec`. |
| `GAS_API_TOKEN` | The same authentication token registered in Apps Script. |
| `SIM_PROVIDER` | `1` for the included 1NCE SIM. |
| `ONE_NCE_APN` | The APN assigned to the included SIM. |
| `SEND_INTERVAL_MS` | `600000UL` (10 minutes). |

### Upload to AP03B

Keep the batteries disconnected and **connect the AZ01C USB-C leaf to your computer with the USB cable**.

1. Set `upload_port` and `upload_command` in `platformio.ini` to match your computer's connection port and STM32CubeProgrammer location. Refer to the [OS-specific configuration examples](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/#3-configure-platformioini), and use the **`leafony_ap03b`** environment for this kit.
2. Open the PlatformIO terminal in VS Code and build the program.

   ```sh
   pio run -e leafony_ap03b
   ```

3. Set AP03B's **PG switch to Program** and press the **RST button**. Then upload with the following command:

   ```sh
   pio run -e leafony_ap03b -t upload
   ```

4. After the upload succeeds, return the **PG switch to Run**.

See the [AP03B documentation](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03b/) for the switch location.

## 6. Check operation

1. Keep the USB cable connected and open the serial monitor with the following command:

   ```sh
   pio device monitor -e leafony_ap03b -b 115200
   ```

2. Press AP03B's **RST button** to start the program. Wait for it to connect to the cellular network and acquire the time.
3. When **`Saved to Google Sheets`** appears in the serial monitor, open the Google spreadsheet.
4. **If a row containing the reception timestamp, temperature, and humidity has been added to the `temperature` sheet, the sample is working.** Leave it running to add new measurements every 10 minutes.

Reception timestamps are recorded in UTC. Add nine hours to read them in Japan Standard Time.

If no row is added, check the settings for the message shown in the serial monitor using [Serial logs and troubleshooting](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/ac09_google_sheets/#troubleshooting).

## 7. Next steps

### Run on batteries away from your computer

1. Disconnect the USB cable and turn the AV06 power switch OFF.
2. Insert two AA batteries into the included battery holder, checking the positive and negative orientation. Connect the holder's PH connector to AV06.
3. Make sure AP03B's PG switch is set to Run, then turn the AV06 power switch ON.
4. Check that a new row is added to the spreadsheet.

Keep the USB cable disconnected when running on batteries. See the [AV06 documentation](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av06/#switch-and-connector) for the power switch and connector locations.

### Use the recorded data and customize the program

- **Chart changes in temperature and humidity**: Select the timestamp, temperature, and humidity columns in the spreadsheet, then choose “Insert” → “Chart”.
- **Change the recording interval**: Change `SEND_INTERVAL_MS` and upload the program again. See [Sample configuration](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/ac09_google_sheets/#configuration) for the allowed range.
- **Learn how to reduce battery consumption**: [Low-power design](https://docs.leafony.com/en/lowpower/) explains communication intervals and sleep modes.

---

# ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit / Kit 2 Getting Started Guide

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/esp32/

Try the Wi-Fi-equipped Leaf!

Use the preinstalled AP02 ESP32 demo to display touch-sensor readings in a phone or computer browser over Wi-Fi. No program upload or development environment is needed. This guide uses three AAA batteries. Before using an 18650 holder instead, check the [battery requirements](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az68/).

## Leaves included in the kit

The following leaves are shared by ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit and Kit 2.

Accessories differ between kits. Check the complete contents of [ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit (Japanese)](https://docs.leafony.com/products/esp32/#%E5%86%85%E5%AE%B9%E7%89%A9) or [ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit 2 (Japanese)](https://docs.leafony.com/products/esp32_2/#%E5%86%85%E5%AE%B9%E7%89%A9).

## What to prepare

- ESP32 Wi-Fi Kit / Kit 2 with the demo still installed
- Three AAA alkaline batteries and the kit's holder
- A Wi-Fi-enabled phone or computer with a web browser

## Usage

1. Install three AAA batteries as shown and turn the power switch ON.

2. On the phone or computer, connect to Wi-Fi with SSID **Leafony_ESP32-AP** and password **password**. This connection is directly to Leafony; internet access is not needed for the demo. If asked whether to stay connected without internet, keep this connection.
3. Enter **`http://192.168.4.1`** in the browser's address bar, including `http://`.
4. Identify pin **26** on the 29pin header using the picture, then touch it. The value decreases when touched. At 20 or lower, **Touch detected** appears.

The demo displays touch inputs on pins 7, 9, 22, 26 and 28. Pin 24 is omitted because it conflicts with RTC & microSD. Once the page appears and pin 26 changes the reading, the initial check is complete. If updates are stopped, select **1 second** or reload the page.

The magnet attached to the kit's Nut Plate lets you mount it on a metal surface.

## Troubleshooting

Follow the [ESP32 Wi-Fi checks](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#esp32-wifi) for the stage that fails: network discovery, connection, page display or sensor readings. If you uploaded another program, use [Restore the demo](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/#restore-demo).

## Next steps

The [Wi-Fi touch sensor example](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/esp32-mcu/esp32/wifi_touchsensor/) explains how to upload the source and change the detection threshold. Use [development environment setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) when you are ready to change the program.

# STM32 MCU Getting Started Guide

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/stm32/

Choose a development tool for STM32 MCU, review the preparation overview, and find setup guides and your first examples.

Start developing with the STM32 MCU leaf (AP03). Choose a tool below to find its setup guide.

:::note[Trying the Basic Kit 2 factory demo]
To try the demo without changing its program, follow the [Basic Kit 2 Getting Started Guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/basic2/). Uploading a new program overwrites the factory demo stored on AP03.
:::

## What to prepare

This is a summary of the preparation shared by the guides for uploading through a USB leaf. Check your chosen environment guide and sample page for the detailed configuration and assembly diagram.

- [AP03 STM32 MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03/)
- A PC running Windows, macOS, or Linux, with an internet connection
- A USB leaf and a data cable that fits its connector
- Sensors, power leaves, and mounting parts specified by your chosen sample

If you have Basic Kit 2, check which processor is fitted. Stop all power supplies, including USB, batteries, and external power, before changing leaves.

For the equipment needed to use a debugger, see [How to connect the debugger](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/stm32_debug/).

## How to write a program

The Arduino IDE and PlatformIO guides linked above describe board configuration, uploading, and checking the result. For STM32CubeIDE, the English guide covers installation; project creation and upload instructions are available in the [Japanese STM32CubeIDE guide](https://docs.leafony.com/environment/stm32/stm32cube_ide/).

Start with the check program in the guide for your tool. Once the development environment is working, move on to sensor and communication examples.

See the [AP03 Program / Run and Reset illustrated guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03/#program-run) for switch positions, LED states and the operation sequence.

## What to try next

The following examples are written for Arduino IDE. Each sample page lists its required leaves, libraries, code, and expected result.

- [Temperature and humidity sensor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/basic/temp_humid_sensors/): display temperature and humidity on your PC
- [Illuminance sensor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/basic/illum_sensor/): measure ambient light
- [Accelerometer](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/basic/accelerometer/): observe changes as the leaf tilts or moves
- [STM32 Logger Beacon](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/stm32_logger_ble_beacon/): try data logging and BLE transmission

For existing projects in PlatformIO, also follow the sample project instructions in the [PlatformIO guide](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/).

## If you need help

Start with your development environment guide and the [FAQ](https://docs.leafony.com/en/faq/). The [AP03 technical reference](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03/) shows switch locations and pin assignments.

If the issue continues, [contact us](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ask/) with your leaf model numbers, development tools, steps tried, and the complete error message.

# Combining Leaves and Choosing a Power Supply

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/

Check the MCU and software, power supply, GPIO and communication pins, I2C addresses, and component clearance when combining Leafony leaves.

When adding a sensor or communication leaf, check **MCU and program → power → pin usage → I2C addresses → component layout**, in that order. Find the functions you need in the [leaf reference](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/) and open each leaf's specifications and examples.

Matching bus contacts do not mean that every leaf can be used simultaneously. The following steps help you assess a configuration; they are not a guarantee of operation or a compatibility matrix for every product.

## 1. Choose the MCU and Program

Start with the leaves, libraries, and development environment specified in an [example](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/). Even when model names are similar, changing the MCU or sensor may require changes to the program.

| What to check | Example |
| --- | --- |
| MCU model and board settings | Distinguish AP01, AP03, AP03B, AP02, and other models, and check the MCU's [development environment](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) |
| Sensor model and library | [AI05](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/) uses different sensors from AI01, so AI01 examples cannot be used unchanged |
| Upload method and interface leaf | Uploading to AP01 through [AZ01C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/) requires a manual reset |
| Signal changes between revisions | [AP03B](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03b/) disconnects D9 from the MCU when BOOT0 is High |

## 2. Choose the Power Supply

Choose a power supply by battery input voltage, output voltage, connector, and the current required by the load. Distinguish **peak current**, such as during communication startup, from **average current**, which affects battery life.

| What to check | Reference and notes |
| --- | --- |
| Battery type and input range | Check specifications for [AV01 CR2032](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av01/) or [AV06 1.8V–5.5V](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av06/) |
| Peak current during wireless communication | [AC08 LTE-M Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac08/) specifies AV06 because its peak current is 400mA |
| Battery and connector | AV06 uses JST PH; AV04 uses JST SH. Check which power leaf the battery holder connects to |
| USB and battery used together | Read the [AZ01C power-state explanation](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/) and check simultaneous supply conditions on the other power leaf too |
| Current estimation and measurement | See [Low-Power Design](https://docs.leafony.com/en/lowpower/) and [Current Measurement with AX05B](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05b/) |

A power IC's maximum output current alone does not tell you whether the connected battery can supply it. Check the battery specifications and the voltage and load conditions you will use. Configurations with both USB and a battery also require checking the power paths.

## 3. Compare GPIO and Communication Pins

Compare the [Leafony Bus contact table](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leafony-bus/) with each leaf's pin assignment. GPIO means general-purpose input/output; a leaf may use these pins for UART, SPI, interrupts, or power control.

1. List the inputs, outputs, and signal names used by each leaf.
2. If leaves use the same bus contact, check whether the signal can be shared and whether separately controlled outputs would conflict.
3. Match MCU port names to the pin assignments and communication ports in the program.
4. Check each device's input/output voltages against the connected device's allowed conditions. Do not confuse the power input voltage range with the allowable GPIO voltage.

The [Pin Assignment Editor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/pinout-editor/) can display and save pin usage for up to eight leaves. It does not determine whether a connection is valid. Blank entries in a preset do not guarantee that a contact is unused or available for another purpose.

## 4. Check I2C Addresses and Pull-Ups

When leaves are stacked, I2C devices connected to SDA/SCL share the same bus. Use the [I2C Address Map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/) to compare addresses, distinguishing standard components, optional components, and reserved addresses.

| Example combination | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| AI05 and AX06 | The LIS2DW12 and I/O expander both use `0x18` |
| Any two of AC04, AC08, and AC09 | Control I/O expanders share address `0x21` |
| Multiple power leaves | Some configurations share battery voltage monitor address `0x50`. Check competing power sources separately |

Do not assume that devices with the same address can be connected unchanged and controlled individually. Whether an address can be changed depends on the device and its assembly.

Check the I2C pull-up resistors too. For example, AI05's R18 and R19 are not fitted; an AI05/AP03 configuration uses AP03's pull-ups. With another MCU or external circuit, check the pull-up voltage and resistors in each circuit.

## 5. Check Clearance and Stacking Order

Even when leaves share the same bus, tall components or battery holders may touch an adjacent leaf. Follow the example's stacking order and insert an [AX04 Spacer](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax04/) where specified.

For communication leaves, also allow access to the antenna position, SIM slot, USB connector, and other connections. See [Assembling and Replacing Leaves](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/assembly/) for assembly steps.

## Record and Test Your Configuration

Test sensors and communication individually with basic examples before running your intended program on a new configuration. Record the following so that the result can be reproduced.

| Item | What to record |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | Leaf models and revisions, stacking order from top to bottom, spacers, and connection photos |
| Power | Battery or USB source, voltage, and power switch positions |
| Software | Example version, board settings, libraries, and pin assignments |
| Results | Sensor readings or communication logs, measured current, and steps that caused problems |

If some conditions remain unclear, [contact us](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ask/) with your configuration and the checks you have tried.

---

# Measure Current and Reduce Power Consumption

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/measuring-power/

Define the measurement boundary and power paths, connect an AX05B and current meter, record an active/transmit/sleep cycle, and compare average current.

Estimating battery life and reducing power consumption requires current measurements over time, including sleep, rather than just active peaks. This guide explains how to measure current on the leaf side with [AX05B I Meas](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05b/) and compare changes under the same conditions.

For calculation methods, see [Low-Power Design and Battery Runtime](https://docs.leafony.com/en/lowpower/). This is a measurement guide; it does not report measured current or battery life for a particular configuration.

## 1. Decide What to Measure

| Question | Measurement location | What it includes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Effect of changing MCU or sensor settings | AX05B V33 line, with the target above and the power source below | Current through the instrument to the upper leaves on the 3.3V line |
| Current drawn by circuits using VBUS | AX05B VBUS line | Current through the instrument on the VBUS line |
| Total consumption seen by the battery | Between the battery and power leaf | Battery-side current, including power conversion losses |

**Current on the 3.3V line is not the same as battery current.** It also excludes circuits below AX05B and any unmeasured power paths. Evaluating battery runtime requires a battery-side measurement or a calculation that accounts for power conversion.

## 2. Check Power Paths and Instrument Mode

The following current path applies when measuring V33 supplied by a power leaf through AX05B. Disconnect all power before changing wiring.

```text
Battery → power leaf (below AX05B)
        → AX05B V33IN → current meter → AX05B V33OUT
        → MCU, sensor, and communication leaves under test (above AX05B)
```

Nordic Power Profiler Kit II (PPK2) has an **Ampere Meter** mode for measuring an external supply and a **Source Meter (SMU)** mode in which the instrument supplies power. The power source and wiring differ between these modes. See the [manufacturer's power supply and mode documentation](https://docs.nordicsemi.com/r/bundle/ug_ppk2/page/ug/ppk/ppk_power_supply.html).

| Mode | Power source | Use in this guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ampere Meter | An external source, such as a battery and power leaf | Insert the current meter in series in the path above |
| Source Meter (SMU) | PPK2 | A different configuration. Define the output voltage and load, disconnect other paths supplying that load, and follow the manufacturer's connection procedure |

The remaining steps use **Ampere Meter** mode. Do not switch modes while retaining the same connected wiring.

## 3. Connect the Current Meter to AX05B

For soldering, pin numbers, and connection photos, see the [AX05B measurement procedure](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05b/).

| PPK2 | AX05B J1 (V33) |
| --- | --- |
| VIN | V33IN (pin 3) |
| VOUT | V33OUT (pin 2) |
| GND | GND (pin 1 or 4) |

- Route the measured V33 line through the current meter between IN and OUT. A parallel jumper would bypass the instrument.
- For the unmeasured VBUS line, connect IN to OUT with a jumper as described in the AX05B procedure. However, if VBUS supplies power to the target, V33 current alone does not represent its total current.
- A power source such as a USB leaf above AX05B may create a path that bypasses the current meter. When measuring battery operation, remove unneeded supplies such as the Leafony USB connection. **Distinguish this from the USB connection that powers PPK2 itself.**
- Check that voltage and current are within the instrument's input limits, and confirm that inserting the meter does not cause resets or communication failures.

Also see the manufacturer's [connector descriptions](https://docs.nordicsemi.com/r/bundle/ug_ppk2/page/ug/ppk/ppk_user_guide_connectors.html) and [Ampere Meter procedure](https://docs.nordicsemi.com/r/bundle/ug_ppk2/page/ug/ppk/measure_current_ampere_meter.html).

## 4. Record a Complete Active and Sleep Cycle

1. Record leaf models, revisions, stacking order, firmware version, instrument, supply voltage, measurement date, and temperature.
2. Record startup and network connection activity after power-on. Keeping initial startup separate from steady operation makes comparisons clearer.
3. During steady operation, record **wake → sensor reading → transmission → sleep → next wake**. Do not calculate an average using only low-current periods.
4. Confirm that sensing and communication succeed using logs or received data. If retries or other events change the cycle length, record multiple cycles.
5. Save the comparison interval duration, average current, peak current, and trace.

## 5. Compare Averages over the Same Interval

If current can be treated as constant within each state, calculate the time-weighted average below. If it varies, use the average of the full interval recorded by the instrument.

```text
Average current = Σ(current in each state × time in that state) / total recorded time
```

If voltage changes, average voltage multiplied by current over time to obtain average power. Do not directly compare 3.3V-side and battery-side currents; use the same measurement location and supply conditions.

| Condition | Comparison interval | Average current | Peak current | Sensing and transmission successful? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Before change | Fill in after measurement | Fill in after measurement | Fill in after measurement | Fill in after checking |
| After change | Fill in after measurement | Fill in after measurement | Fill in after measurement | Fill in after checking |

## 6. Change One Setting at a Time

Change just one setting, such as the measurement interval, radio transmission interval, unused sensor sleep mode, or MCU clock frequency. Refer to the [energy reduction techniques](https://docs.leafony.com/en/lowpower/#reduce-energy-use) and repeat the measurement at the same location, voltage, and comparison interval.

A lower average current, while retaining the required measurement frequency, successful communication, and responsiveness, demonstrates an improvement under those conditions. Verify final battery runtime by operating the device with the intended battery, temperature, and communication conditions.

# Leaf Reference

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/

Find leaf specifications by what you can do: measurement, communication, display, and more.

Find specifications and connections by kit or function. To choose products to buy, see the [kits and products page](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/). Check the [shop](https://shop.leafony.com/collections/products) for prices, availability, and planned releases.

This reference also includes leaves supplied in kits and documentation for discontinued leaves.

See the [glossary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/) for abbreviations and connector terminology.

When adding a leaf, use the [guide to combining leaves](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/) and [assembly basics](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/assembly/) to check power, pins, and fastening. Documentation status describes the readiness of instructions, separately from product availability.

## Browse by kit

## Processors

Run programs to read sensors and control other leaves. Uses an ATmega328P with digital I/O, PWM outputs, and analog inputs.

  Read sensors and control other leaves with a 32-bit STM32 microcontroller. Use a USB leaf for USB connections or a Shield leaf for SWD connections.

  Read sensors and control other leaves. A redesigned version of AP03, equipped with an STM32L452REI6.

  An MCU leaf intended for evaluating image processing and edge AI. Uses an STMicroelectronics STM32N6-series microcontroller.

## Communication

Combine with an MCU leaf to send and receive sensor data and other information over Bluetooth LE. Uses a Silicon Labs BGM11S22F256GA-V2 module with Japanese radio certification.

  Combine with an MCU leaf to exchange data with compatible devices over LoRa radio. Uses a Murata Type ABZ module and a STAF chip antenna covered by Japanese radio design certification.

  Combine with an MCU leaf to send and receive data using Cat-M1, an IoT cellular communication technology that runs on mobile operators' LTE networks. Requires an AV06 power leaf, a compatible SIM, and a mobile service contract. Uses a Murata Type 1SC module and a certified chip antenna.

  A leaf for data communication over Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 networks. Includes a Taiyo Yuden WSCLxADAH2Z-series module, a nanoSIM slot, and a U.FL connector for an external antenna.

## I/O

Measure temperature, humidity, and light, and use acceleration to detect tilt or movement. Combine with an MCU leaf to monitor the surrounding environment or the movement of an attached object.

  Measure temperature, humidity, pressure, and 3-axis acceleration. The standard configuration uses a BME280 and LIS2DW12, read over I2C by an MCU leaf.

## Power

Supply 3.3V to the leaves from a CR2032 coin cell. An MCU can read battery voltage, and a power switch turns the supply on or off.

  Supply 3.3V at up to 1A from a 1.8V–5.5V battery connected through a PH connector. An MCU can read the battery voltage.

  A power leaf for supplying power and charging using a solar panel.

## Extension

Connect Arduino Shields to add functions, or attach SWD/ICSP tools. Includes Arduino Shield connectors and three leaf interfaces.

  Connect leaf signals to external circuits for prototyping and signal checks. Breaks out all 29 leaf interface pins to 2.54mm-pitch through holes.

  Connect external circuits for prototyping and signal checks. Breaks out the 29 Leafony Bus pins to 2.54mm-pitch through-hole pads.

  Increase the spacing between stacked leaves to prevent components from touching.

  Connect an external current meter to measure current on the Leafony Bus V33 and VBUS lines. Inserts the instrument in series with the power line.

## Other Leaves and Accessories

Connect this leaf to upload sketches to an AVR MCU or use the serial monitor. It uses an FTDI FT232RQ USB-to-UART converter. A step-down circuit converts USB VBUS (5V) to 3.3V, supplying both VBUS and 3.3V to the leaves.
The successor is AZ01C USB-C. Uploading to AP01 through AZ01C requires a manual reset.

  Connect to a computer through USB Type-C for serial communication and 3.3V power to the leaves. Uploading a program to AP01 requires a manual reset.

  Electrically connect stacked leaves. Place ACR (anisotropic conductive rubber) between the leaves and compress it with screws to make contact.

  The Connector Cover protects the ACR (anisotropic conductive rubber) from dirt.

  The Nut Plate secures leaves with screws. Do not use ordinary hex nuts, as they may touch board contacts and cause a short circuit.

  Houses Basic Kit and attaches to a magnetic surface using the magnet on its base.

## Discontinued

Run programs and send or receive data over Wi-Fi or Bluetooth LE. Uses an ESP32-WROOM-32 with Japanese radio certification, and supports uploading sketches over USB.

  Send and receive data over LoRa radio. This leaf is discontinued. Its successor is AC07 LoRa Mary, which changes the MCU interface from UART to SPI.

  Combine with an STM32 MCU to send and receive data over Wi-Fi. AVR MCU is not supported. This leaf is discontinued.

  Send and receive data using cellular communication. Requires AC05, a compatible SIM, and a mobile service contract. This leaf is discontinued. The successor cellular configuration uses AC08 LTE-M Mary and the AV06 power leaf.

  Combine with LTE-M King M to supply power, upload programs to the MCU, and read battery voltage. This leaf is discontinued. For a new cellular configuration, see AC08 LTE-M Mary and the AV06 power leaf.

  Detect an approaching person and play sound through a speaker. An MCU can control actions such as playing a melody when someone approaches.

  Read ambient sound or a potentiometer setting, and light an LED. An MCU can use these readings to produce an indication based on sound level.

  Display text or numbers on an 8-character × 2-line LCD and accept input from two switches. The reference page includes power setup, libraries, and a text-display quickstart.

  Supply 3.3V to the leaves from a CR2450 coin cell and read battery voltage through an MCU. Includes a power switch.

  Supply 3.3V to the leaves from AA batteries and read battery voltage through an MCU. Includes a battery holder and power switch.

  Supply 3.3V to the leaves from a battery connected through an SH connector. An MCU can also read the battery voltage.

  A connector leaf for arranging leaves side by side.

  Connect an external ammeter to measure current on the 3.3V and VBUS lines.

  Connect 5V Grove modules. Supports UART, I2C, analog input, and digital input.

  A connector leaf for connecting leaves back to back.

  Connect leaf signals to external circuits through pin headers. Breaks out all 29 leaf interface pins at a 2.54mm pitch.

  Read the time and store data on a separately purchased microSD card. Combine with an MCU to record measurements with timestamps.

  Connect AAA batteries to the AV04 power leaf. Includes a JST SH connector.

  Connect an 18650 battery to the AV04 power leaf. Fits a battery measuring 18mm in diameter and 65mm in length, and includes a JST SH connector.

# Communication

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/

Choose a leaf to view its specifications, pin assignments and technical documents.

- [AC02 BLE Sugar](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac02/): Send and receive data with compatible smartphones or computers over BLE.
- [AC03 LoRa Easy](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac03/): Send and receive data with a compatible remote device over LoRa radio. Discontinued; its successor is [AC07 LoRa Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac07/). The MCU interface changes from UART to SPI.
- [AC07 LoRa Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac07/): Send and receive messages or sensor data over LoRa radio with an MCU leaf and a compatible device at the other end.
- [AC08 LTE-M Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac08/): Send and receive data over a cellular network with an MCU leaf, a compatible SIM card and a communication service contract. Requires [AV06 1.8V–5.5V (Japanese)](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/power/av06/) for its 400mA peak current.
- [AC09 Cat-M1 TY](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/): Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 leaf for cellular data communication with a processor leaf. Supported operators, tested SIM cards and other requirements will be announced once confirmed.

See also the [leaf reference index](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/) and [I²C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/).

# AC02 BLE Sugar

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac02/

## Features

Send and receive data wirelessly with compatible smartphones or computers using [BLE (Bluetooth Low Energy)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#ble). Combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf and a sensor leaf, this leaf can send sensor measurements to a receiving device.

It uses Silicon Labs' certified BGM11S22F256GA-V2 BLE module and connects to the MCU leaf via [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart). Radio certifications include CE, FCC, ISED Canada, TELEC, KC South-Korea, and NCC Taiwan (SLICON LABS Module Data Sheet Revision 1.2).

| Bluetooth version | 4.2                                               |
| Frequency range   | 2400M ~ 2483.5MHz                                 |
| RX sensitivity    | -90 dBm @ 1 Mbit/s GFSK                           |
| TX power          | +8dBm以下                                         |
| RF certification  |  CE, full FCC, ISED Canada, Japan and South-Korea |
| Flash             | 256KB                                             |
| RAM               | 32KB                                              |
| Interfaces        | UART                                              |
| Dimension         | W23×D20.5×H4.7mm                                  |

# AC03 LoRa Easy

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac03/

**This leaf has been discontinued. Its successor is [AC07 LoRa Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac07/).**

The microcontroller interface changes from [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart) on AC03 to [SPI](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#spi) on AC07. When migrating, check the connection instructions and libraries documented for AC07.

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac03/ac03a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac03/ac03a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac03/ac03a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Send and receive data over LoRa radio with a compatible device at a remote location. Combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf and a sensor leaf, this leaf can transmit sensor measurements. Set up devices at both the transmitting and receiving ends.

It uses EASEL's certified ES920LRA1 LoRa module and connects to the MCU leaf via [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart).

## Specification

| Item                                              | Description                |
| :------------------------------------------------ | :------------------------- |
| Part Number                                       | ES920LRA1                  |
| SoC                                               | MKL16Z128 (ARM Cortex-M0+) |
| RF Transceiver                                    | SX1276 (SEMTECH)           |
| Frequency range                                   | 920.6～928.0MHz            |
| Transmission speed                                | 146bps～22kbps             |
| RX sensitivity                                    | -118～-142dBm              |
| TX power                                          | Max 13dBm（20mW)           |
| RF certification                                  | TELEC                      |
| Approximate communication distance (wire antenna) | Prospect 5km               |
| Flash                                             | 128KB                      |
| RAM                                               | 32KB                       |
| Interfaces                                        | UART                       |
| Dimension                                         | W23×D32.8×H4.6mm           |

## Tips
### Stacking a leaf directly above this leaf
This leaf uses components that are 2 mm or taller. Placing another leaf directly above it without a spacer may result in a poor electrical connection. Always insert an AX04 Spacer between this leaf and the leaf above it.

# AC07 LoRa Mary

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac07/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac07/ac07_f_small.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac07/ac07_b_small.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac07/ac07_p_small.jpg)

## Features

Send and receive messages or sensor data over LoRa radio when combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf. Prepare a compatible device at the other end of the link for low-power wireless communication.

This LoRa leaf uses a Murata Type ABZ module and a chip antenna (STAF 1019-085A) with Japanese radio equipment construction design certification. It comes programmed with firmware [v1.2.3](https://github.com/arduino/mkrwan1300-fw/releases/tag/1.2.3), published for the Arduino MKR WAN 1300/1310, so you can program it with Arduino.

## Specifications

| Item | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| Part number | CMWX1ZZABZ-091 |
| Chipset | SX1276, STM32L072CZ |
| Secure element | ATECC608A |
| Carrier frequency | 920MHz band (920.6 MHz to 928 MHz), Japan |
| Modulation method | LoRa™ modulation |
| Antenna | [Murata antenna support (Japanese)](https://www.murata.com/ja-jp/products/connectivitymodule/lpwa/design-development/antenna-support) |
| Interface | SPI |
| RF certification | FCC, IC, TELEC, KCC |
| Dimensions | W23 × D30 × H2mm |

## LoRaWAN and private LoRa

LoRaWAN and private LoRa both use LoRa modulation for wireless communication, but their upper MAC layers differ. LoRaWAN is a standard developed by the LoRa Alliance that supports interoperability between devices from different manufacturers and wide-area communication. Private LoRa uses a proprietary MAC-layer protocol and requires a dedicated gateway, with no communication fees. See the following references for more information.

- [Differences between LoRaWAN and private LoRa (Japanese)](https://easel5.com/technical-guide/difference-lorawan-and-private-lora/)
- [The Arduino Guide to LoRa® and LoRaWAN®](https://docs.arduino.cc/learn/communication/lorawan-101/)

## Board layout

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac07/ap07_fig1.jpg)

The Molex 73412-0110 is compatible with the U.FL RF coaxial connector developed by Hirose Electric.

## Antennas

LoRa Mary has a chip antenna (1019-085A) with Japanese radio equipment construction design certification. For longer-range communication, attach an external antenna.[^1] The antennas below have this certification. See [Murata antenna support (Japanese)](https://www.murata.com/ja-jp/products/connectivitymodule/lpwa/design-development/antenna-support) for details.

| Model | Supplier | Antenna type | Connector | Dimensions | Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1019-085A[^2] | STAF Corporation | Monopole (λ/4) | | 4 × 9.1 × 1.2mm | Chip antenna |
| 1018-504B[^2] | STAF Corporation | Dipole (λ/2) | U.FL | 100 × 13 mm (cable length 140mm) | FPC antenna |
| 1019-008A | STAF Corporation | Monopole (λ/2) | SMA[^3] | Length 160mm, diameter 9mm | External antenna |

[^1]: The chip antenna and external antenna cannot be used together. To use an external antenna, reposition the 0Ω resistor.
[^2]: These antennas are certified even though they are not included in Murata's recommended antenna list.
[^3]: SMA stands for SUB-MINIATURE TYPE A and is a MIL-standard connector. Use a U.FL-to-SMA adapter cable to connect it to LoRa Mary.

## Tips

### Programming firmware with STLINK and STM32CubeProgrammer

1. Prepare the following:
   - LoRa Mary, Shield and screws
   - A 3.3V power supply, or USB for power
   - STLINK-V3SET
   - A computer and USB cable
2. Secure LoRa Mary and USB (for power) to the Shield with screws, then connect the STLINK-V3SET. See [Connecting the debugger](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/stm32_debug/) for details.
3. Start STM32CubeProgrammer.
4. Select `ST-Link` as the connection on the right, set `Frequency(KHz)` to `8000`, and click `Connect`.
5. Open the erase and programming panel on the left and configure the following:
   - File path: select the v1.2.3 `.bin` file.
   - Enable programming verification.
6. Click `Start Programming`. Programming is complete when `Download verified successfully` appears.

### Programming firmware with FP-10 and C-Flash

1. Prepare the following:
   - LoRa Mary, Shield and screws
   - A 3.3V power supply, or USB for power
   - [computex FP-10](https://www.computex.co.jp/products/fp_10/index.htm?_fsi=evfJ0avn)
   - A computer and USB cable
2. Download C-Flash:
   - Enter the `CODE` and `SERIAL NO` printed on the FP-10 at the [C-Flash download page](https://www.computex.co.jp/support/download/cd/logon), then download the software.[^4]
3. Load the program into the FP-10:
   - Connect the FP-10 to the computer and start C-Flash.
   - Click `設定` (Settings) → `ターゲット設定` (Target settings).
   - Select the manufacturer to narrow down the microcontroller list, choose the `STM32L07xxZ` filter, and click `起動する` (Start).
   - On the initial settings tab, set the target to `未接続` (Not connected), and select `SWD` and `1MHz` for the interface.
   - Click `ファイル` (File) → `ロード` (Load) → `追加` (Add), then select the v1.2.3 `.bin` file.
   - Set the load address to `0x08000000`, which is the Flash start address.
   - Select `データ` (Data) → `書き込み` (Write) to load the program into the FP-10.
4. Program LoRa Mary:
   - Connect the FP-10 to a USB AC adapter.
   - Secure LoRa Mary and USB to the Shield with screws, then connect to an AC adapter.
   - Connect the FP-10 to the Shield's SWD interface.
   - Press the FP-10 `PROGRAM` button. The `STS` LED lights when programming succeeds.

[^4]: See the [setup video (Japanese)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bex7SuHc1Cg) for download and licensing instructions.

### Spreading factor (SF) and bandwidth (BW)

SF describes how much the transmitted data is spread. The LoRa library accepts values from 6 to 12, with SF7 as the default. SF6 requires implicit header mode for both transmission and reception. See the [LoRa library API](https://github.com/Leafony/arduino-LoRa/blob/master/API.md#spreading-factor) for details. The main characteristics are shown below.

| SF | Characteristics |
| :--- | :--- |
| SF6–SF8 | Shorter communication range and higher data rate |
| SF10–SF12 | Longer communication range and lower data rate |

BW is the width of the frequency band. Common values are 125kHz, 250kHz and 500kHz, with 125kHz as the default. The main characteristics are shown below.

| Bandwidth | Characteristics |
| :--- | :--- |
| Narrow (125kHz) | Lower data rate, longer communication range and lower power consumption |
| Wide (500kHz) | Higher data rate, shorter communication range and higher power consumption |
