# AC08 LTE-M Mary

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac08/

## Features

Send and receive data when combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf, using Cat-M1, an IoT cellular communication technology that runs on mobile operators' LTE networks. Add a sensor leaf to send measurements. A compatible SIM card and a communication service contract are required.

This cellular leaf uses a Murata Type 1SC module and a chip antenna (STAF 1019-085A) with Japanese radio equipment construction design certification. It connects to the MCU leaf over [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart). A library is available to help you program LTE-M Mary.

**Use [AV06 1.8V–5.5V](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av06/), because this leaf has a peak current of 400mA.**

| Item | Description |

| Operating voltage | 2.85–4.35V |
| Transmit current at 23dBm | 400mA |
| Antenna | Onboard chip antenna (STAF 1019-085A) |
| SIM card | nanoSIM |
| Interface | UART |
| Baud rate | 115200 bps |
| Dimensions | W23 × D32 × H2mm |

The `151TEMP` and `713TEMP` suffixes indicate different production lots. The module itself is the same.

## AT commands

AT commands are standardized by 3GPP, an international organization for cellular communication standards, and let you configure modem operation and connections. Command specifications differ between modems, so consult the manufacturer's AT command manual. The following procedure uses SORACOM as an example.

### What to prepare

- [LBAD0XX1SC-DM-EVK-B](https://www.murata.com/ja-jp/products/connectivitymodule/cat-m1/support)
- A computer running Windows or macOS
- A standard-size SIM card (for example, SORACOM plan-D)
- [APN settings (Japanese)](https://support.soracom.io/hc/ja/articles/218427317-APN-%E8%A8%AD%E5%AE%9A%E3%81%A8%E3%81%AF%E4%BD%95%E3%81%A7%E3%81%99%E3%81%8B-%E4%BD%95%E3%82%92%E8%A8%AD%E5%AE%9A%E3%81%97%E3%81%BE%E3%81%99%E3%81%8B):
  - APN: `soracom.io`
  - Username: `sora`
  - Password: `sora`
  - PDP type: `IP`
  - Authentication: CHAP or PAP
- [MCC (Mobile Country Code) and MNC (Mobile Network Code) (Japanese)](https://support.soracom.io/hc/ja/articles/115001760231-SORACOM-Air-for-%E3%82%BB%E3%83%AB%E3%83%A9%E3%83%BC%E3%81%A7%E3%81%AF%E3%83%87%E3%83%90%E3%82%A4%E3%82%B9%E3%81%8B%E3%82%89-Cell-ID-%E3%81%A8-Location-Area-Code-%E3%82%92%E5%8F%96%E5%BE%97%E3%81%A7%E3%81%8D%E3%81%BE%E3%81%99%E3%81%8B)

| Type | plan-D | plan-KM1 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| MCC | 440 | 440 |
| MNC | 10 | 51 |

### AT command basics

AT commands usually start with `AT`, followed by `<command>` and, in some cases, `<value>`. There are four types: **Set**, **Read**, **Test** and **Execute**.

| Type | Syntax | Example | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Set | `AT+<command>=<value>` | `AT+COPS=1,2,<MCCMNC>` | Manually connect to a network operator |
| Read | `AT+<command>?` | `AT+COPS?` | Check the current network operator |
| Test | `AT+<command>=?` | `AT+COPS=?` | Search for available network operators |
| Execute | `AT+<x>` | `AT+CSQ` | Check signal strength and connection quality as numeric values |

### Before you start

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+CFUN=1,1` | `OK` | Reset the modem to its default state |
| `AT+CPIN?` | `+CPIN: READY``OK` | Check the SIM card |

### Query device information

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+CGMM` | `LBAD0XX1SC-DM``OK` | Check the modem hardware |
| `AT+CGMR` | `RK_03_02_00_00_41841_001``OK` | Check the modem firmware version |
| `AT+CIMI` | `440103198454299``OK` | Check the IMSI (International Mobile Subscriber Identity) |

### Network operator and cellular technology settings (SORACOM plan-D)

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+COPS=?` | `+COPS: (1,"NTT DOCOMO","DOCOMO","44010",7),(0,"KDDI","KDDI","44050",7),(3,"KDDI","KDDI","44052",7),(0,"KDDI","KDDI","44054",7),(0,"KDDI","KDDI","44051",7),(0,"SoftBank","SoftBank","44020",7),,(0-3),(0-2)``OK` | Search for available network operators |
| `AT+COPS?` | `+COPS: 0``OK` | Check the network connection |
| `AT+COPS=1,2,44010` | `OK` | Connect to NTT DOCOMO manually |
| `AT+COPS=0` | `OK` | Connect automatically |
| `AT+COPS?` | `+COPS: 0,2,"44010",7``OK` | Check the network connection |
| `AT+COPS=1,2,44010` | `OK` | Connect to NTT DOCOMO manually |

### Define the cellular band

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT%SETSYSCFG="SW_CFG.catm_band_table.band#1","ENABLE;19"` | `OK` | Set Band 19 in band#1 |
| `AT%GETSYSCFG="SW_CFG.catm_band_table.band#1"` | `%GETSYSCFG: "SW_CFG.catm_band_table.band#1","ENABLE;19"``OK` | Check the band#1 setting (Band 19) |
| `AT%SETSYSCFG="SW_CFG.catm_band_table.band#1",""` | `OK` | Clear the band#1 setting |

### Check radio signal strength and quality

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+CSQ` | `+CSQ: 17,99``OK` | Check signal strength and quality |

### Network configuration

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+CGDCONT=1,"IP","soracom.io"` | `OK` | Connect to SORACOM |
| `AT+CGDCONT?` | `+CGDCONT: 1,"IP","soracom.io",10.242.227.27,0,0,0,0,0,,0,,,,``OK` | Check the APN connection |
| `AT+CGACT?` | `+CGACT: 1,0``OK` | PDP context is inactive |
| `AT+CGACT=1,1` | `OK` | Configure the PDP context |
| `AT+CGACT?` | `+CGACT: 1,1``OK` | PDP context is active |
| `AT+CEREG?` | `+CEREG: 0,1``OK` | Registered on the network |

### Check the FPLMN

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+CRSM=176,28539,0,0,12` | `+CRSM: 144,0,"FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"``OK` | |

### Clear the FPLMN

| AT command | Example response | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `AT+CRSM=214,28539,0,0,12,"FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"` | `+CRSM: 144,0``OK` | |
| `AT+CGPADDR` | `+CGPADDR: 1,"10.242.227.27"``OK` | |

## Revision history

- September 2026: Updated the fitted module part number to 151TEMP and clarified the part number difference between production lots.
- August 2024: Initial version.

# AC09 Cat-M1 TY

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/

Specifications, pin assignment and development documents for the AC09 leaf with a Taiyo Yuden Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 module

These photos show the AC09 board. The front side has the Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 module and external antenna connector; the back side has the nanoSIM slot.

## Features

This Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 leaf is intended to provide cellular data communication for IoT devices when combined with a processor leaf. The [Google Sheets example](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/#related-samples) for the Cat-M1 Kit's AP03B + AI05 configuration includes SIM and endpoint settings. Distinguish the example requirements from product-wide operator support and guaranteed operation.

AC09 Cat-M1 TY uses a Taiyo Yuden WSCLxADAH2Z-series cellular LPWA module.

- Communicates with the module over [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart). An [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c) I/O expander controls the power-button, shutdown and wakeup signals.
- Includes a nanoSIM slot, an onboard chip antenna and a U.FL connector for an external antenna.
- The module supports low-power operation with eDRX and PSM. See [Taiyo Yuden's product information (Japanese)](https://www.yuden.co.jp/jp/product/solutions/lpwa/) for details.

### Module, antenna connector and SIM slot locations

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac09/ac09-component-locations.svg)

1. **Communication module (front)**. Provides Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 communication.
2. **External antenna connector (front)**. This is a U.FL connector. See [Antennas](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/#antennas) for the conditions for selecting the onboard or external antenna.
3. **nanoSIM slot (back)**. This slot accepts a nanoSIM compatible with the cellular service you use.

Click the diagram to enlarge it. Arrows identify the components; they do not show the SIM insertion direction. See [Cat-M1 Kit development preparation](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/cellular-lpwa-cat-m1/) for SIM and endpoint settings.

## Specifications

| Item | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 module | Taiyo Yuden WSCLxADAH2Z series |
| Communication technology | Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 |
| Power input | Leafony Bus 3.3V terminal (pin 1) |
| Host interfaces | UART (TX/RX, RTS/CTS), I2C (control) |
| UART level shifter | TXB0104RUTR (3.3V / 1.8V) |
| I/O expander | PCAL6408AHKX |
| I2C address | 0x21 (7-bit notation) |
| SIM card | nanoSIM (Molex 1042240820 slot) |
| Onboard antenna | STAF 1019-085A |
| External antenna connector | Hirose Electric U.FL-R-SMT-1(10) |
| Board dimensions | 23 × 38.7 mm (design dimensions, excluding component height) |

Product specifications, including the exact module part number, the full range of supported bands and operators, and current consumption, will be announced once confirmed. The related example describes 1NCE and SORACOM settings; it does not guarantee operation with every SIM, region or leaf configuration.

## Power and control

The Leafony Bus 3.3V terminal supplies the module's VBAT input. An onboard TPS61021ADSGT generates the RF power supply (VBAT_FEM), and a TLV71718PDQNT generates the 1.8V signal-circuit supply (VDDIO).

The module's power state is controlled through the I/O expander. The [published sample](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/ac09_google_sheets/) uses AV06 as a battery-powered configuration example. Also see the [power-supply Q&A](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ac09-voltage/).

## Pin assignment

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/communication/ac09/ac09-pinout-en.svg)

Click the diagram to enlarge it. MCU denotes the processor leaf, and arrows show the direction of UART signals. RESET and INT_N are the reset and interrupt signals of the PCAL6408A I/O expander.

Select AC09 in the [Pin Assignment Editor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/pinout-editor/) to edit the same diagram and save it as PNG or SVG.

The following table lists the main Leafony Bus signals used by AC09. UART directions are shown from the processor leaf's perspective.

| Pin | Leafony Bus signal | AC09 connection or function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 3.3V | Power input (VBAT) |
| 5 | RESET | I/O expander reset |
| 7 | D6 | UART input: receives the module's RTS signal (processor CTS) |
| 11 | D8 | UART transmit: connects to the module's RX |
| 13 | D9 | UART receive: input from the module's TX |
| 22 | D2 | I/O expander interrupt output (INT) |
| 23 | SDA | I2C data |
| 25 | SCL | I2C clock |
| 26 | D4 | UART output: sends to the module's CTS (processor RTS) |
| 27 | GND | Power and signal ground |

### I2C address

The I/O expander address is **0x21**. [AC08 Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac08/) and AC04 King M use the same address, so connecting these leaves to the same I2C bus causes an address conflict. Check the [I2C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/) when combining leaves.

## Antennas

The board is designed to select either the onboard chip antenna (ANT1) or the external antenna U.FL connector (CN3) through the JP1 connection.

| JP1 connection | Antenna used |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1–2 | Onboard chip antenna (STAF 1019-085A) |
| 2–3 | External antenna connected to CN3 |

Supported antennas and certification conditions will be announced once confirmed. Documents about antennas covered by the module's certification are available under “Reference アンテナ一覧” on [Taiyo Yuden's product page (Japanese)](https://www.yuden.co.jp/jp/product/solutions/lpwa/). User registration is required.

## Development environment and samples

The [PlatformIO projects in the AC09 development repository](https://github.com/leafony/ac09-cat-m1-ty/tree/main/platformio) contain development code using STM32 MCU leaves and the Arduino framework. See [Documents](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/#documents) for repository access requirements.

| Project | Purpose and configuration |
| --- | --- |
| `google_sheets` | Uses the Cat-M1 Kit's AP03B + AI05 to read BME280 temperature and humidity and record them in Google Sheets. Select environment `leafony_ap03b` |
| `http_get` | Checks HTTP communication with AP03 |
| `mqtt_thingspeak` | Sends AP03 + AI01 measurements to ThingSpeak over MQTT |

Check each project's README for settings and required software.

For AT command specifications, see the “AT command manual (Light Version)” on [Taiyo Yuden's product page (Japanese)](https://www.yuden.co.jp/jp/product/solutions/lpwa/). User registration is required.

### Related samples

- [Save temperature and humidity data to Google Sheets with AC09 Cat-M1 TY](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/ac09_google_sheets/): Uses AP03B to read temperature and humidity from the AI05 Env Sensors leaf and record them in Google Sheets. The Docs guide sets the transmission interval to 10 minutes; the GitHub development template uses 30 seconds.

[Cat-M1 Kit development preparation](https://docs.leafony.com/en/getting-started/cellular-lpwa-cat-m1/) covers assembly and sample settings.

# Extension

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/

Connect external circuits, change how leaves are arranged, or measure current with an external instrument. Choose a leaf below for its specifications, pin assignments and technical documents.

- [AX01 Shield](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax01/) — Connect Arduino Shields and SWD or ICSP programming tools.
- [AX02 29 pin](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax02/) — Connect external circuits to the 29 leaf interface pins using through-hole pads.
- [AX02B 29-pin](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax02b/) — Prototype circuits and check signals using 2.54 mm pitch through-hole pads.
- [AX03 Leaf x2](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax03/) — Connect leaves side by side.
- [AX04 Spacer](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax04/) — Add space between stacked leaves to prevent component interference.
- [AX05 I Meas](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05/) — Measure current on the 3.3 V and VBUS lines with an external ammeter.
- [AX05B I Meas](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05b/) — Measure current on the V33 and VBUS lines with an external instrument. Includes illustrated connection and measurement instructions for the PPK2.
- [AX06 Grove&5V](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax06/) — Connect 5 V Grove modules for UART, I2C, analog or digital inputs.
- [AX07 Back to back](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax07/) — Reverse the orientation of connected leaves.
- [AX08 29pin header](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax08/) — Connect external circuits or test equipment using pin headers.

See also the [leaf reference index](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/) and [I²C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/).

# AX02B 29-pin

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax02b/

These photos show the AX02B board from the front, back, and an angle.

## Features

Connect leaf signal and power lines to external circuits for prototyping and signal checks. This leaf brings all 29 pins of the Leafony Bus out to 2.54 mm pitch through-hole pads, allowing connections to breadboards or universal boards using [jumper wires](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#jumper-wire) or pin headers.

AX02B is a minor revision of [AX02 29 pin](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax02/) with changes to the PCB layout and silkscreen. It uses the same schematic as AX02 and is electrically compatible.

- Converts the 29 pins of the Leafony Bus to 2.54 mm pitch through-hole pads
- Leafony standard 20 mm square leaf shape

## Specification

| Item | Description |
| :--- | :---------- |
| Board dimensions | W20×D20mm |
| Pin pitch | 2.54mm |

## Pin assignment

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax02b/ax02b-pinout-en.svg)

“Port” in the diagram indicates the through-hole number connected to each Leafony Bus pin.

Viewed from the back side, where the pin numbers are printed, with the Leafony Bus contacts at the top, the pin numbers advance downward in groups of five from the upper left. The through-holes are arranged in six columns and five rows, with the bottom-right hole not connected (NC). Viewed from the front side, which has the connector, the layout is mirrored left to right: pin 1 is at the upper right and the unconnected hole is at the lower left.

| Column | Pins |
| :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 |
| 2 | 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 |
| 3 | 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 |
| 4 | 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 |
| 5 | 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 |
| 6 | 26, 27, 28, 29, NC (not connected) |

In the KiCad schematic, Leafony Bus `F1` through `F29` are connected to the through-hole pads.

For Leafony Bus pin assignment data, see [Leaf-pinassign](https://github.com/Leafony/Documents/tree/main/Leaf-pinassign).

## Documents

Refer to the following dedicated files for the AX02B layout and silkscreen.

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin)
- [Schematic (PDF)](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/blob/main/output/schematic.pdf)
- [PCB layout (PDF)](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/blob/main/output/layout.pdf)
- [KiCad project](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/tree/main/kicad/ax02-29-pin)
- [Schematic (KiCad)](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/blob/main/kicad/ax02-29-pin/ax02-29-pin.kicad_sch)
- [PCB layout (KiCad)](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/blob/main/kicad/ax02-29-pin/ax02-29-pin.kicad_pcb)
- [Manufacturing data](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/tree/main/kicad/ax02-29-pin/Gerber)
- [Panelized manufacturing data](https://github.com/leafony/ax02b-29-pin/tree/main/kicad/ax02-29-pin/panelized/Gerber)

# AX05 I Meas

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05/

:::note[Discontinued product and successor]
AX05 I Meas is discontinued. Its successor is [AX05B I Meas](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05b/). See the successor's page for external current meter connections and measurement instructions.
:::

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05/ax05a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05/ax05a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05/ax05a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

This leaf can measure the current consumption of 3.3V and VBUS. In the current measurement leaf, the pads on the front and back sides of the 3.3V and VBUS are electrically separated, so by connecting an ammeter to each of the following through holes, the total power supply current of a single leaf or a group of leaves located far from the battery leaf can be measured. In the example below, the sensor leaf and the BLE leaf are located on the far side of the battery leaf via the current measurement leaf, so the total current of both leaves can be measured.

## Specification

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W23×D20.5×H4.7mm             |

# AX05B I Meas Current Measurement Leaf

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax05b/

| Top | Bottom |
| --- | --- |
| [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/top.jpg) | [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/bottom.jpg) |

## Features

Leafony AX05B I Meas is a leaf for measuring current on the `V33` and `VBUS` lines of the Leafony Bus. It separates each power line into `IN` and `OUT` so an external current measurement instrument, such as the Nordic Power Profiler Kit II (PPK2), can be inserted in series.

It separates the power supply connections of the leaves stacked below AX05B from those stacked above it, allowing you to measure the current flowing to the upper leaves.

Each power line coming from the lower leaves is split into `IN` and `OUT` on AX05B. Connect the current measurement instrument in series on the line you want to measure, and short `IN` and `OUT` with a jumper on the line you are not measuring.

- Supports current measurement on the Leafony Bus `V33` and `VBUS` lines
- Provides 2.54 mm pitch right-angle pin headers for both `V33` and `VBUS`
- Power lines that are not being measured can be shorted with jumpers for normal use

## Specification

| Item | Description |
| :--- | :---------- |
| Dimension | W20×D20mm |
| Board thickness | 0.8mm |
| Layer | 2 layers |
| Surface finish | ENIG (Immersion gold) |
| Bus connector | Leafony Bus (F29/B29) |
| Measurement connector | 1×4, 2.54 mm pitch, right-angle pin header ×2 |

## Package contents

AX05B I Meas includes the board, two single-row four-pin right-angle pin headers, and two jumper pins.

| Board | Included parts |
| :--- | :--- |
| [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/contents-1.jpg) | [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/contents-2.jpg) |

## Measurement connector

`J1` is for `V33`, and `J2` is for `VBUS`. Both connectors use the same pin assignment.

| Pin | J1 (V33) | J2 (VBUS) | Use |
| :--- | :------- | :-------- | :-- |
| 1 | `GND` | `GND` | Measurement instrument GND |
| 2 | `V33OUT` | `VBUSOUT` | Current flowing out to the top side of the leaf |
| 3 | `V33IN` | `VBUSIN` | Current flowing in from the bottom side of the leaf |
| 4 | `GND` | `GND` | Measurement instrument GND |

## Current measurement with Nordic Power Profiler Kit II

The Nordic Power Profiler Kit II (PPK2) is a current logger that can measure both the tiny currents drawn by low-power IoT devices during sleep and the milliamp-level currents drawn while they are active. It can also operate as a source measurement unit (SMU), providing power while measuring current.

This makes it a useful tool for developing battery-powered IoT devices, including Leafony applications.

Follow these steps to measure current with the PPK2.

1. Solder the included single-row four-pin headers onto the leaf as shown below.

   [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/soldered.jpg)

2. Connect the PPK2 pins to the `V33` connector as shown in the table. To insert the PPK2 as an ammeter in series with the power line, connect `VIN` to `V33IN` and `VOUT` to `V33OUT`.

   | PPK2 | AX05B J1 (V33) | Use |
   | :--- | :--- | :--- |
   | `GND` | `GND` | GND |
   | `VIN` | `V33IN` | Power coming from the lower leaves |
   | `VOUT` | `V33OUT` | Power going to the upper leaves |
   | `GND` | `GND` | GND |

   [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/ppk2-connection.jpg)

   [](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax05b/v33-current-flow.svg)

   Place AX05B between the lower leaves and the upper leaves you want to measure. The `V33` supply from the lower leaves passes through the ammeter connected to AX05B before reaching the upper leaves. When using a single ammeter, such as the PPK2, short the unmeasured `VBUS` line with a jumper pin so that power reaches the upper leaves.

3. Since `VBUS` is not being measured in this example, short `VBUSIN` and `VBUSOUT` with one of the included jumper pins.
4. Assemble the stack with the leaves whose current you want to measure above AX05B and all other leaves below it.
5. Turn on the power, operate the PPK2 in ammeter mode, and click **Start** to begin measuring current. In the Power Profiler app, this mode is called **Ampere meter**, as shown in the [official PPK2 quick start](https://docs.nordicsemi.com/r/bundle/ug_ppk2/page/ug/ppk/ppk_user_guide_quick_start.html).

For information on using the PPK2, see the [official page (Japanese)](https://www.nordicsemi.jp/tools/ppk2/).

## Documents

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure)
- [KiCad project](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure/tree/main/kicad)
- [Schematic (PDF)](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure/blob/main/output/schematic.pdf)
- [PCB layout (PDF)](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure/blob/main/output/layout.pdf)
- [Schematic (KiCad)](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure/blob/main/kicad/leafony-ax05b.kicad_sch)
- [PCB layout (KiCad)](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure/blob/main/kicad/leafony-ax05b.kicad_pcb)
- [Panelized manufacturing data](https://github.com/leafony/ax05b-current-measure/tree/main/kicad/panelized/Gerber)

# AX06 Grove&5V

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax06/

## Features

Connect 5 V Grove-compatible sensors and other modules to Leafony for [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart) or [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c) communication and analog or digital inputs. This leaf supports the Seeed Studio Grove series and boosts 3.3 V to 5 V to power the connected modules. The I2C expander lets you turn off the 5 V supply to reduce power consumption while the modules are not in use.

# AX07 Back to back

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax07/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax07/ax07a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax07/ax07a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax07/ax07a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Connect a leaf with its front and back orientation reversed. This expansion leaf keeps all leaf interface terminals connected while allowing a leaf to face the opposite direction.

## Specification

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W29×D17×H4.7mm 　            |

# AX08 29pin header

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax08/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax08/ax08a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax08/ax08a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/extension/ax08/ax08a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Use [jumper wires](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#jumper-wire) or similar connections to link leaves to external circuits or test equipment for prototyping and signal checks. This leaf brings all 29 pins of the leaf interface out to pin headers.

## Specification

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W30×D20.5×H10.6mm 　          |

# I2C Address Map

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/

List of I2C device addresses used on each leaf

This page lists the I2C devices mounted on each leaf and their slave addresses. All addresses are in 7-bit notation.

When multiple leaves are stacked, all of their I2C devices share the same I2C bus (SDA/SCL) on the Leafony Bus. Stacking leaves that use the same address causes bus conflicts, so check the combination before use. When using I2C devices on a [home-made leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb), design it so that its addresses do not overlap with the table below, including the reserved addresses.

## Address Map

Cellular communication (Cat-M1) in the table is an IoT communication technology that runs on mobile operators' LTE networks.

| Address | Device | Part Number | Leaf | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0x18 | I/O expander | PCA9557RGVR | [AX06 Grove&5V](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/extension/ax06) | ON/OFF control of the 5V Grove power supply |
| 0x18 | Accelerometer | LIS2DW12TR | [AI05 Env Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/) | SDO/SA0 tied to GND. Conflicts with AX06 |
| 0x19 | Accelerometer | LIS2DHTR | [AI01 4-Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai01) | |
| 0x1A | I/O expander | PCA9557RGVR | [AI04 LCD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04) | LCD power control and switch input. 0x1E is reserved |
| 0x1B | I/O expander | PCA9557RGVR | [AI03 MIC&VR&LED](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai03) | Power ON/OFF control |
| 0x21 | I/O expander | TCA6408ARSVR | [AC04 LTE-M King M](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac04) | Cellular (Cat-M1) module control. 0x20 is reserved |
| 0x21 | I/O expander | PCAL6408AHKX | [AC08 LTE-M Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac08) | Cellular (Cat-M1) module control |
| 0x21 | I/O expander | PCAL6408AHKX | [AC09 Cat-M1 TY](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac09/) | Cellular LPWA Cat-M1 module control |
| 0x3E | Character LCD | AQM0802A | [AI04 LCD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04) | |
| 0x40 | I/O expander | TCA9536ADTMR | [AC06 Wi-Fi Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac06) | Wi-Fi module control |
| 0x41 | I/O expander | TCA9536DGKR | [AC07 LoRa Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac07) | LoRa module control |
| 0x43 | I/O expander | TCA9536BDTMR | [AV05 Solar Charger](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av05) | |
| 0x44 | Temperature/humidity sensor | SHT40-AD1B-R2 | [AI05 Env Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/) | Optional; not fitted in the standard configuration. Conflicts with AI01's reserved address |
| 0x45 | Illuminance sensor | OPT3001 | [AI01 4-Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai01) | 0x44 is reserved |
| 0x50 | A/D converter | ADC081C027CIMK | [AV01](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av01)–[AV04](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av04), [AV06](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av06) (power leaves) | Battery voltage monitor. 0x51 and 0x52 are reserved |
| 0x50 | A/D converter | ADC101C027CIMK | [AC05 LTE-M King S](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac05) | Battery voltage monitor. 0x51 and 0x52 are reserved |
| 0x50 | A/D converter | ADC101C027CIMK | [AV05 Solar Charger](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av05) | Battery voltage monitor. 0x51 and 0x52 are reserved |
| 0x59 | VOC gas sensor | SGP40-D-R4 | [AI05 Env Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/) | Optional; not fitted in the standard configuration |
| 0x5F | Temperature/humidity sensor | HTS221TR | [AI01 4-Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai01) | |
| 0x60 | Secure element | ATECC608A | [AC07 LoRa Mary](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/communication/ac07) | |
| 0x65 | Human detection sensor | AK9754AE | [AI02 SP&PIR](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai02) | 0x66 is reserved |
| 0x68 | RTC | PCF8523TK | [AZ02 RTC&microSD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az02) | |
| 0x76 | Temperature/humidity/pressure sensor / gas sensor | BME280 / BME680 | [AI05 Env Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/) | BME280 is standard; BME680 is an alternative. Fit only one |

Note: AC04–AC06, AI02–AI04, AV02–AV04, AX06, and AZ02 are discontinued products.

## Remarks

- The AI05 Env Sensors LIS2DW12 and the AX06 Grove&5V I/O expander share `0x18`. Do not connect them to the same bus with their standard settings.
- If the optional SHT40 is fitted to AI05, its `0x44` conflicts with a selectable address of AI01's illuminance sensor. AI05 and AI01 also share the D3 interrupt line, so do not use them together without modifications.
- Address 0x50 of the battery-monitoring A/D converter is shared by the power leaves (AV01–AV04, AV06), AC05 LTE-M King S, and AV05 Solar Charger. If these leaves are stacked together, the A/D converters cannot be read individually.
- Address 0x21 is shared by AC04 LTE-M King M, AC08 LTE-M Mary, and AC09 Cat-M1 TY. Connecting them to the same I2C bus causes an address conflict and prevents individual control of their I/O expanders.
- The reserved addresses (0x1E, 0x20, 0x44, 0x51, 0x52, 0x66) are alternate addresses selectable by the address pins of the devices above. Do not use them on home-made leaves either.

## Related Links

- [Home-made leaf development](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb)
- [I2C address map (GitHub: Leafony/Documents)](https://github.com/Leafony/Documents/tree/main/I2C%20address%20map)

# IO

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/

Combine these leaves with an MCU leaf to measure your surroundings, accept input, or control outputs. Choose a leaf to view its specifications, pin assignments and technical documents.

- [AI01 4-Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai01/): Measure temperature, humidity, ambient light, and acceleration.
- [AI02 SP&PIR](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai02/): Detect an approaching person and play sounds or melodies.
- [AI03 MIC&VR&LED](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai03/): Capture ambient sound, read the potentiometer setting, and control LEDs.
- [AI04 LCD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04/): Display text and numbers on an 8-character, 2-line LCD and read two switches.
- [AI05 Env Sensors](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/): Measure temperature, humidity, pressure, and 3-axis acceleration with a BME280 and LIS2DW12 in the standard configuration.
- [AIx1 Motor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/aix1/): Drive two DC motors with a motor power supply within the specified voltage and current limits.

See also the [leaf reference index](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/) and [I²C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/).

---

# AI01 4-Sensors: Temperature, Humidity, Light and Acceleration

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai01/

Explore Leafony AI01 sensor ranges, I2C addresses and pin assignments for HTS221TR, OPT3001 and LIS2DHTR, with AVR, ESP32 and STM32 code examples.

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai01/ai01a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai01/ai01a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai01/ai01a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Measure temperature, humidity, ambient light (illuminance), and acceleration. Combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf, this leaf lets you read changes in the surrounding environment and the leaf's movement.

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai01/ai01-stack-context.jpg)

The AI01 4-Sensors leaf is shown on the right. The left shows an example stack with MCU, communication, power, and other leaves. Click the figure to enlarge it. The Japanese labels identify the Leafony stack and the separate 4-Sensors leaf.

It has a temperature/humidity sensor, an illuminance sensor, and an accelerometer. The MCU leaf reads their measurements over [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c).

### Sensor locations

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai01/ai01-sensor-locations.jpg)

The arrows identify the accelerometer (加速度), temperature/humidity sensor (温湿度), and illuminance sensor (照度). The specifications below list the sensor chips and their measurement ranges.

## Specification

### Dimension

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W23×D20.5×H4.7mm             |

### Temperature/Humidity Sensor

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Part  number                   | HTS221TR                     |
| Relative Temperature range     | -40～120℃                   |
| Temperature accuracy           | ±0.5°C (15 to +40°C)         |
| Relative humidity range        | 0 to 100%                    |
| Humidity accuracy              | 3.5% rH (20 to +80% rH)      |
| Interfaces                     | I2C(Address: 0x5F)           |

### Illuminance Sensor

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Part  number                   | OPT3001                      |
| Measurement range              | 0.01 lux to 83 k lux         |
| IR Rejects                     | > 99% (typ)                  |
| Interfaces                     | I2C(Address: 0x44 or 0x45)   |

### Acceleration Sensor

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Part  number                   | LIS2DHTR                      |
| Measurement range              | ±2g/±4g/±8g/±16g (selectable) |
| Function                       | 6D/4D orientation detection   |
| Freefall detection             |                               |
| Motion detection               |                               |
| Interfaces                     | I2C(Address: 0x19)            |

# AI02 SP&PIR

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai02/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai02/ai02a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai02/ai02a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai02/ai02a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf, this leaf lets you detect an approaching person and play sounds or melodies. A sample demonstrates playing a melody when someone approaches.

It has a piezoelectric speaker connected to the MCU leaf through [PWM](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#pwm) and an IR sensor connected over [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c). The sensor has a built-in proximity detection algorithm and can be configured to output an interrupt signal when it detects an approach.

## Specification

### Dimension

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W23×D20.5×H5.3mm             |

### Piezoelectric Speaker

| Item                 | Description                                      |
| :------------------- | :----------------------------------------------- |
| Part number          | CMT-1203-SMT                                     |
| dimensions           | 12 x 12 x 3mm                                    |
| rated frequency      | 4kHz(typ)                                        |
| sound pressure level | 81dB(min) at 10 cm, 5 Vp-p, 4,000 Hz square wave |
| Current consumption  | 5mA(max) at 5 Vp-p, 4,000 Hz square wave         |

### IR Sensor

| Item                       | Description                                                              |
| :------------------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Part number                | AK9754                                                                   |
| Sensor                     | Quantum-type IR Sensor                                                   |
| Interfaces                 | I2C(Address: 0x65 or 0x64)                                               |

# AI03 MIC&VR&LED

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai03/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai03/ai03a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai03/ai03a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai03/ai03a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Capture ambient sound with the microphone, read the potentiometer setting, and turn the LED on or off. Combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf, this leaf can be used in programs that read changes in sound.

The [MEMS](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mems) microphone and potentiometer connect to the MCU leaf's analog input pins, and the LED connects to a digital output pin. To reduce power consumption, you can turn off the power through a load switch controlled by the [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c) Expander.

## Specification

### Dimension

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W23×D20.5×H4.7mm             |

### Microphone

| Item            | Description     |
| :-------------- | :-------------- |
| Part number     | SPW2430HR5H-B   |
| Type            | MEMS            |
| Direction       | Omnidirectional |
| Frequency range | 100Hz ～ 10kHz  |
| Gain            | 0dB             |
| Interfaces      | Analog          |

### Volume

| Item                       | Description    |
| :------------------------- | :------------- |
| Part number                | ST-4ETA10kΩ    |
| Nominal resistance         | 10kΩ           |
| Resistance law             | Linear law (B) |
| Effective electrical angle | 210° (1 turn)  |

### LED

| Item           | Description |
| :------------- | :---------- |
| Part number    | SML-A12Y8TT86 |
| Package type   | Side-view   |
| Emitting color | Yellow      |

### I2C I/O Expander

| Item         | Description         |
| :----------- | :------------------ |
| Part number  | PCA9557RGVR         |
| Interface    | I2C (Address: 0x1B) |

# AI04 LCD

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai04/ai04a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai04/ai04a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai04/ai04a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Combined with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf, this leaf lets you display text and numbers on the [LCD (liquid crystal display)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#lcd) and accept input from two switches. Add a sensor leaf to view its measurements on the display.

The LCD unit connects to the MCU leaf over [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c). One switch connects to an MCU digital input pin, and the other connects to the I2C Expander's P1 pin. To reduce power consumption, you can turn off LCD power through a load switch controlled by the I2C Expander.

The display has **8 characters per line and 2 lines**. `Hello, World!` (13 characters) does not fit on one line.

:::note[Documentation for a discontinued leaf]
AI04 is discontinued. To use a leaf you already own, refer to the specifications and samples on this page, and the spec sheet and schematic linked below.
:::

## Specification

### Dimension

|              Item              |         Description          |
| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |
| Dimension     　               | W30.8×D30.5×H5.3mm             |

| Viewing area (WxH)    | 27x10.5mm                          |
| Dot size (WxH)        | 0.45x0.5mm                         |
| Dot pitch (WxH)       | 0.5x0.55mm                         |
| Character size (WxH)  | 2.45x4.35mm                        |
| Character pitch (WxH) | 2.95x4.9mm                         |
| Viewing direction     | 6:00 O'Clock                       |

| Item         | Description                 |
| :----------- | :-------------------------- |

| Interface    | I2C (Address: 0x1A or 0x1E) |

## Pinassign

## Tips
### Powering and initializing the LCD

**Enable LCD power through the I2C I/O Expander before initializing the LCD.** Calling `lcd.begin()` alone does not operate the leaf's power switch.

| Device | 7-bit I2C address | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| I2C I/O Expander (PCA9557) | `0x1A` or `0x1E` | LCD power control and switch input |
| LCD controller (ST7032) | `0x3E` | Display settings and character data |

The [AVR LCD sample](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/avr-mcu/exten/lcd/) uses expander address `0x1A` and performs these steps:

1. Start I2C with `Wire.begin()`.
2. Configure P0 as an output with `i2c_write_byte(0x1A, 0x03, 0xFE)`.
3. Enable LCD power with `i2c_write_byte(0x1A, 0x01, 0x01)`.
4. Call `lcd.begin(8, 2)`, `lcd.setContrast(30)` and `lcd.clear()` in that order, then display text.

`i2c_write_byte()` is a function defined in the sample. Use the linked page for the complete sketch. If your expander responds at `0x1E`, set the sample's `I2C_EXPANDER_ADDR` to that address.

### I2C responds, but the display is blank

Finding an address with an I2C scan or successfully sending a command does not establish that LCD power, initialization and contrast are ready for display. First check the power steps above and try the sample with its specified library. The sample intentionally turns LCD power off for 3 seconds, during which the display goes blank.

When controlling the ST7032 directly without the library, follow the [datasheet initialization procedure](https://akizukidenshi.com/goodsaffix/ST7032-0Dv1_3.pdf#page=33), including the delay after power becomes stable, instruction-table selection, contrast, power and follower settings, and delays between commands. The linked library enables the follower and waits 200 ms inside `begin()`, then sets contrast and enables the booster in `setContrast()` ([library implementation](https://github.com/tomozh/arduino_ST7032/blob/master/ST7032.cpp)). Copying isolated commands can leave out required settings or delays.

### About the switch

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai04/ai04_tips.jpg)

| Item    | Description                      |
| :------ | :------------------------------- |
| Switch1 | Connected to pin 2               |
| Switch2 | Connected to I2C Expander P1 pin |

# AI05 Env Sensors

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/

AI05 specifications and connections, with AP03 PlatformIO examples for sensor readings, motion interrupts, and 100-sample FIFO capture and waveform display after a shock.

These photos show the AI05 board from the front, back, and an angle.

## Features

This leaf measures temperature, humidity, pressure and 3-axis acceleration. Combine it with an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf to read environmental conditions and the leaf's tilt and motion.

The standard configuration uses a **BME280** temperature, humidity and pressure sensor and a **LIS2DW12** 3-axis accelerometer. It operates from the Leafony Bus 3.3 V supply, and readings are obtained over [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c). A four-pin connector is available for external I2C devices.

Pads are also provided for SHT40, SGP40 and BME680 sensors. These are not fitted as standard. Using them requires the components and program described under [optional assembly](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/#optional-assembly).

### Sensor and external pad locations

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai05/ai05-component-locations.svg)

1. **Temperature, humidity and pressure: BME280 (U3)**. This environmental sensor is fitted as standard.
2. **3-axis acceleration: LIS2DW12 (U5)**. Use it to read tilt and motion.
3. **External I2C connection: J1**. These four pads bring out 3.3 V, GND, SDA and SCL. See [External I2C connector J1](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/#external-i2c-connector-j1) for the pin order.

Click the diagram to enlarge it. The empty pads for additional sensors in the photo are unpopulated as standard. Gas measurements require the components and matching program described under [optional assembly](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/#optional-assembly).

## Specifications

### Board and interfaces

| Item | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Board dimensions | 23 × 20 mm |
| Board thickness | 0.8 mm (excluding component height) |
| Board layers | 4 |
| Power and signal voltage | 3.3 V |
| Communication | I2C, up to 400 kHz |
| Acceleration interrupt | LIS2DW12 INT1 connected to Leafony Bus D3 |
| External connector J1 | 4 pins, 2.54 mm pitch, for a right-angle pin header |
| SDA/SCL pull-ups | R18 and R19 (2.7 kΩ each) are not fitted as standard |

### Standard configuration

| Reference | Part | Manufacturer | Measurements |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| U3 | BME280 | Bosch Sensortec | Temperature, humidity and pressure |
| U5 | LIS2DW12TR | STMicroelectronics | 3-axis acceleration |

The BME280 operating temperature range is −40 to 85 °C, and the pressure measurement range is 300 to 1100 hPa. Accuracy conditions depend on temperature; see the [BME280 manufacturer documentation](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/en/products/environmental-sensors/humidity-sensors-bme280).

The LIS2DW12 acceleration range can be set to ±2 g, ±4 g, ±8 g or ±16 g ([manufacturer documentation](https://www.st.com/en/mems-and-sensors/lis2dw12.html)).

### Optional assembly

DNP (Do Not Populate) means the component is not fitted.

| Reference | Part | Function | Standard configuration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| U1 | SHT40-AD1B-R2 | Temperature and humidity | DNP |
| U2 | SGP40-D-R4 | Gas sensor responding to volatile organic compounds (VOCs) | DNP |
| U4 | BME680 | Temperature, humidity, pressure and gas sensor | DNP |

The BME280 (U3) and BME680 (U4) have separate footprints, but **only one is fitted**. Both use I2C address `0x76`, so they cannot both be fitted and read independently.

The standard configuration populates U3, C21 and C22, leaving U4, C23 and C24 unpopulated. Reverse that choice to use BME680. SHT40 and SGP40, which are not fitted as standard, will not respond to an I2C scan.

When adding SHT40, also fit C20. When adding SGP40, also fit R10 (4.7 Ω), C2 and C3. These are also unpopulated as standard; without R10, SGP40 receives no power.

Gas measurement is not included in the standard configuration. Using metrics such as SGP40's VOC Index requires the sensor and corresponding signal processing ([SGP40 manufacturer information](https://sensirion.com/jp/products/catalog/SGP40), [BME680 manufacturer information](https://www.bosch-sensortec.com/en/products/environmental-sensors/gas-sensors/bme680)).

## I2C addresses

All addresses use 7-bit notation.

| Device | Address | Configuration |
| --- | --- | --- |
| LIS2DW12 | `0x18` | Standard; SDO/SA0 connected to GND |
| BME280 | `0x76` | Standard; SDO connected to GND |
| SHT40 | `0x44` | Optional |
| SGP40 | `0x59` | Optional |
| BME680 | `0x76` | Alternative to BME280; SDO connected to GND |

## Pin connections

### Leafony Bus

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai05/ai05-pinout-en.svg)

Click the diagram to enlarge it. F24 is the LIS2DW12 INT1 interrupt output. Select AI05 in the [Pin Assignment Editor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/pcb/pinout-editor/) to edit the same diagram and save it as PNG or SVG.

| Signal | Connector contacts | AI05 function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V33 | F1 / B1 | 3.3 V power |
| SDA | F23 / B23 | I2C data |
| D3 | F24 / B24 | LIS2DW12 INT1 interrupt |
| SCL | F25 / B25 | I2C clock |
| GND | F27 / B27 | Power and signal ground |

F/B are the front/back contact names on the KiCad Leafony Bus connector CN1. LIS2DW12 INT2 is not connected. See the [Leafony Bus](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leafony-bus/) for the overall bus specification.

### External I2C connector J1

| Pin | Signal | Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | GND | Power and signal ground |
| 2 | +3.3V | Leafony Bus 3.3 V supply |
| 3 | SDA | I2C data |
| 4 | SCL | I2C clock |

J1 accepts a four-pin, 2.54 mm pitch header and shares the Leafony Bus power and I2C bus. Check pin numbers and 3.3 V compatibility before attaching cables or external devices.

## Connection requirements

- **Check the I2C pull-ups.** R18 and R19 are not fitted. When paired with AP03 STM32 MCU, the pull-ups on AP03 are used. For other MCUs and external devices, also check that SDA/SCL are pulled up to 3.3 V.
- **The I2C address conflicts with AX06 Grove&5V.** AI05's LIS2DW12 and AX06's I/O expander both use `0x18`. Do not connect them to the same bus with their standard settings.
- **The D3 interrupt line conflicts with AI01 4-Sensors.** AI05 uses acceleration address `0x18` and AI01 uses `0x19`, but the interrupt line is shared, so do not combine them unchanged. If SHT40 is added, `0x44` may also conflict, depending on the address setting of AI01's light sensor.
- Devices connected to J1 also share the I2C bus. Check the [I2C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/) for conflicts with other leaves.

## PCB layout

These reference images were generated from the KiCad board data. They omit component 3D models and include pads for optional components. See [standard configuration](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/#standard-configuration) and [optional assembly](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/#optional-assembly) for fitted and unpopulated components.

## Software

For a complete walkthrough of the regular-reading sample, including measured output, see [Read temperature, humidity, pressure and acceleration with AI05](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/beginner/stm32-mcu/env-sensors/).

PlatformIO + Arduino examples are available for AI05 with the [AP03 STM32 MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03/). Each example is a separate project.

| Example | Behavior | Output to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [read_sensors (Japanese README)](https://github.com/leafony/ai05-env-sensors/tree/main/platformio/read_sensors) | Detects and initializes sensors at startup, then reads them every second | BME280 temperature, humidity and pressure; LIS2DW12 X/Y/Z acceleration |
| [accel_wakeup (Japanese README)](https://github.com/leafony/ai05-env-sensors/tree/main/platformio/accel_wakeup) | Receives LIS2DW12 motion detection interrupts | Time since startup, event count, detected axes and X/Y/Z acceleration |
| [accel_shock_fifo (Japanese README)](https://github.com/leafony/ai05-env-sensors/tree/main/platformio/accel_shock_fifo) | Reads 100 acceleration samples from the FIFO after detecting a shock | Browser plots of X/Y/Z and acceleration magnitude, with CSV export |

All examples use 400 kHz I2C with SDA on AP03 PB9 (D14) and SCL on PB8 (D15). Serial output is 115200 bps; connect to a PC through a USB serial leaf or equivalent interface. **Periodic sensor readings, motion detection interrupts, and capture and waveform display of 100 samples after a shock have been tested on AP03 with a standard AI05.**

### Read sensors periodically

`read_sensors` detects BME280 at `0x76` and LIS2DW12 at `0x18`. It displays temperature in °C, humidity in %RH, pressure in hPa and acceleration in g. Acceleration includes gravity even when the board is stationary. This example does not use the D3 interrupt.

The code also supports optional SHT40, SGP40 and BME680 sensors, and skips sensors that are not fitted. BME280 and BME680 are distinguished by their chip IDs. SGP40 outputs a raw VOC signal (`SRAW_VOC`), and BME680 gas output is a resistance value; the example does not convert these to a VOC Index, IAQ score or ppm.

### Receive motion detection interrupts

`accel_wakeup` receives interrupts through LIS2DW12 INT1 → Leafony Bus D3 → AP03 PB3. No additional wiring is required when connected through Leafony Bus. Defaults are 100 Hz, ±2 g, a motion threshold of 0.250 g and a duration of 20 ms.

Keep the board still during initialization. After `LIS2DW12: ready` and `Move the board...` appear, move the board gently. Lines such as `Wake-up #1` appear, and the event count increases with repeated motion. Measurements are not printed periodically while the board is stationary. The displayed acceleration includes gravity and is read when the event is processed; it is not the peak value at the instant the interrupt occurred. The event count reflects processed interrupts and may differ from the number of physical movements.

This example uses the sensor's Wake-up function. **The MCU keeps running normally; it does not wake from Sleep or Stop mode.** See the example README for sensitivity adjustments.

### Record 100 samples after a shock with the FIFO and view the waveform

`accel_shock_fifo` records 100 acceleration samples when the LIS2DW12 generates a Wake-up interrupt. It uses the same INT1 → D3 → PB3 interrupt path as `accel_wakeup`. Defaults are **400 Hz, ±8 g, and a shock detection threshold of 0.500 g**. The sensor's FIFO, a buffer that stores readings in order, holds 32 samples. The program drains it into RAM repeatedly to collect 100 samples.

Each capture contains **only data acquired after shock detection**. The first sample after the FIFO starts is discarded before saving 100 samples, so the capture is not guaranteed to include the peak at the instant of impact. The MCU continues running normally.

After [building and uploading](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai05/#build-and-upload), run the following command from the repository root to start the supplied waveform viewer. It uses Python 3 and requires no additional packages.

```sh
python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory platformio/accel_shock_fifo/viewer
```

1. Open  in desktop Chrome or Edge.
2. Close the serial monitor, click “シリアル接続” (Connect serial) in the viewer, and select AP03's USB serial port.
3. Set AP03 to Run, press Reset, and keep the board still during initialization. Once “衝撃を待っています” (Waiting for a shock) appears, move the board gently.
4. The waveform appears after all 100 samples arrive. Toggle X/Y/Z and acceleration magnitude as needed, and click “CSVを保存” (Save CSV) to save a capture.

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/ai05/shock-fifo-viewer.png)

This example shows a waveform recorded on hardware in the Japanese viewer interface (100 samples, 400 Hz, ±8 g). The maximum acceleration magnitude in this capture is 5.002 g. You can also reload CSV files and switch between the most recent 20 captures. Without a connected device, “デモを見る” (View demo) displays generated data.

The horizontal axis starts at the first retained sample and shows **estimated times from 0 to 247.5 ms**, calculated from the configured 400 Hz rate. These are neither times relative to shock detection nor measured timestamps for each sample. The displayed acceleration and magnitude include gravity, so the magnitude is approximately 1 g while stationary. The detection threshold applies to the high-pass-filtered signal and cannot be compared directly with the displayed values.

Additional shocks during acquisition, transmission, or the 500 ms waiting period are not saved as separate captures. FIFO overruns, I2C read failures, timeouts, or excessive readout delays invalidate a capture. Captures are kept only in browser memory, so save the required data as CSV before closing the page. See the [example README (Japanese)](https://github.com/leafony/ai05-env-sensors/tree/main/platformio/accel_shock_fifo) for threshold adjustments and error output.

### Build and upload

Download or clone the [repository](https://github.com/leafony/ai05-env-sensors). In VS Code, open the folder containing the `platformio.ini` for the example you want to run. Use the supplied settings (`board = leafony_ap03`). With PlatformIO Core, choose the command for the example you want to build and run it from the repository root:

```sh
pio run -d platformio/read_sensors
pio run -d platformio/accel_wakeup
pio run -d platformio/accel_shock_fifo
```

To upload over USB serial, close the serial monitor and disconnect the waveform viewer, set AP03 to Program and press Reset before uploading. After the upload completes, return to Run, connect either the serial monitor or waveform viewer at 115200 bps, and press Reset. They cannot connect to the same port at the same time. See each example's README (Japanese) for port selection, upload commands and sample output.

AI01 4-Sensors uses different sensors, so its temperature/humidity and acceleration examples cannot be used unchanged.

# AIx1 Motor

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/aix1/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/aix1/aix1a_motor_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/aix1/aix1a_motor_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/aix1/aix1a_motor_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Drive two [DC motors (motors powered by direct current)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#dc) from an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf with the onboard TB6612FNG motor driver. Provide the motors or pump and a motor power supply separately, and connect them through the harness. Check the specifications below for the supported voltage and current.

For example, combine it with a [BLE](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#ble) communication leaf and an electric pump to switch the pump on or off from a compatible smartphone and water plants. See [Watering plants with a motor](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/motor/motor_demo/) for the example.

## Specification

| Item                          | Description |
| :---------------------------- | :---------- |
| Part number                   | TB6612FNG   |
| Motor Supply Voltage          | 2.5V~13.5V  |
| Output current (Vm≧4.5V)      | 1A          |
| Output current (4.5V>Vm≧2.5V) | 0.4A        |
| Dimension                      | W25.6×D30.9×H4.7mm|

## Block diagram
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/aix1/aix1_motor_block.png)

## Pinassign
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/aix1/aix1_motor_pinassign.png)

## Tips
### Harness Connection

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/io/aix1/aix1_motor_tips.jpg)

| Pin  | Description       |
| :--- | :---------------- |
| 1    | Motor A+          |
| 2    | Motor A-          |
| 3    | Motor B-          |
| 4    | Motor B+          |
| 5    | GND               |
| 6    | Motor Supply (Vm) |
| 7    | GND               |
| 8    | 3.3V              |

# Others

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/

Program leaves over USB, read the time, save data, or assemble and protect a leaf stack. Choose an item below for its specifications and technical documents.

- [AZ01 USB](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01/) — Upload sketches to an AVR MCU, use a serial monitor, and supply power over USB. Its successor is [AZ01C USB-C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/); uploading to AP01 through AZ01C requires a manual reset.
- [AZ02 RTC&microSD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az02/) — Read the date and time, and save or read data on a microSD card.
- [AZ61 Connector](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az61/) — Electrically connect signal and power lines between stacked leaves.
- [AZ62 Connector Cover](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az62/) — Protect the connector from dust and debris.
- [AZ63 Nut Plate](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az63/) — Secure leaves with screws.
- [AZ66 Basic kit case](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az66/) — House the Basic Kit and mount it on a surface that magnets stick to.

See also the [leaf reference index](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/) and [I²C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/).

# AZ01 USB

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/others/az01/az01a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/others/az01/az01a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/others/az01/az01a_p_large.jpg)

:::note[Successor leaf]
[AZ01C USB-C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/) is the successor with a USB Type-C connector. Uploading sketches to AP01 through AZ01C requires a manual reset. See the successor's page for connection and upload instructions.
:::

## Features

Upload sketches to an AVR [MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) over USB and view the MCU's output in a serial monitor on your computer. This leaf also supplies power from USB to the other leaves. It uses an FTDI FT232RQ for USB-to-[UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart) conversion and a step-down circuit to generate 3.3 V from USB VBUS (5 V), supplying both VBUS and 3.3 V to the leaves.

| :----------------------------- | :--------------------------- |

| Data transfer rates | 300 baud to 3 Mbaud |

### Power Supply

| Item                   | Description                                                         |
| :--------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------ |

| Output voltage         | 3.3V±2%                                                             |
| Controlling method     | PWM/PFM Automatic switching control                                 |
| Maximum output current | 500mA                                                               |
| Protection circuit     | Over current protection / thermal shutdown/short-circuit protection |

# AZ01C USB-C

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01c/

USB-C to UART and USB power for Leafony, including manual-reset programming with AP01 AVR MCU.

## Overview

Connect a computer to Leafony over USB-C to program the [MCU (microcontroller that runs programs)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu), inspect its output through [UART](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#uart) serial communication, and supply 3.3 V power to the Leafony Bus from USB. Programming AP01 requires the manual reset described below.

AZ01C USB-C is a USB-C to UART leaf and the successor to [AZ01 USB](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az01/). The published design uses the FTDI FT234XD for USB-UART conversion and generates 3.3 V power from USB VBUS.

This page describes the design published in the [leafony/az01c-usb-c repository](https://github.com/leafony/az01c-usb-c). Specifications and components may change in the future.

## Main uses

- Programming the MCU on a Leafony leaf
- UART debugging of Leafony leaves
- Supplying 3.3 V power to the Leafony Bus from USB

## Features

:::caution[AP01 programming requires a manual reset]
AZ01C does not support automatically resetting AP01 when Arduino IDE opens the serial port. Use the AP01 reset switch when uploading. The appearance of a serial port alone does not mean uploading will start automatically.

:::

AZ01C USB-C is a USB-UART leaf with a USB Type-C connector. The TPS6282533 generates 3.3 V from USB VBUS 5 V, then supplies the Leafony Bus 3.3 V rail through a MAX40200AUK+T ideal diode.

The design aims to prevent unnecessary power consumption by the USB-C leaf when USB is disconnected and a battery on another leaf supplies 3.3 V. It limits backfeeding through both the UART signals and the 3.3 V power line. The TS3A4741 physically disconnects TX/RX, while the MAX40200AUK+T blocks reverse current from the 3.3 V power line toward the TPS6282533.

## Published specifications

### Electrical specifications

| Item | Min | Typ | Max | Unit | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| USB VBUS input voltage | 4.5 | 5.0 | 5.5 | V | Used as a USB-C UFP/Sink |
| Buck output voltage P3V3_BUCK | 3.27 | 3.30 | 3.33 | V | TPS6282533 fixed 3.3 V, ±1% accuracy |
| Leafony Bus 3.3 V output | - | 3.26 | - | V | After MAX40200; approximately 43 mV drop at 500 mA |
| Leafony Bus 3.3 V output current | - | - | 500 | mA | TPS6282533 is rated at 2 A and MAX40200 at 1 A; this design limits the output to 500 mA |
| MAX40200 reverse leakage | - | 0.07 | 1.5 | µA | From Leafony Bus +3.3 V toward P3V3_BUCK |
| UART baud rate | 300 | - | 3,000,000 | baud | FT234XD specification |
| UART I/O logic voltage | - | 3.3 | - | V | FT234XD VCCIO connects to the Leafony Bus 3.3 V rail |
| Idle current with USB connected | - | 12 | - | mA | Estimate including FT234XD, buck converter, MAX40200, and LED circuitry |
| Battery-side current with USB disconnected | - | 0.15 | 2.3 | µA | Calculated from the datasheet values for MAX40200 reverse leakage and TS3A4741 standby current; FT234XD operation with VCC=0 V and VCCIO=3.3 V requires hardware verification |
| Operating temperature | -40 | 25 | +85 | ℃ | Common operating range of the components |

### Mechanical specifications

| Item | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| Dimensions | Leafony 20 mm x 20 mm |
| PCB thickness | 0.8 mm recommended |
| Layers | 4 |
| Assembly | Double-sided |
| USB connector | Hirose CX90M-16P |
| External connection | 29-pin Leafony Bus |

### USB specifications

| Item | Specification |
| :--- | :--- |
| USB standard | USB 2.0 Full Speed (12 Mbps) |
| Connector | USB Type-C |
| Type-C role | UFP / Sink Only |
| CC resistors | CC1 and CC2 each pulled down to GND through 5.1 kΩ |
| USB PD | Not supported |
| Drivers | FTDI VCP / D2XX |

## Circuit design

### Power architecture

The TPS6282533 generates the local `P3V3_BUCK` rail from USB VBUS. The MAX40200AUK+T supplies this power to the `+3.3V rail` on the Leafony Bus side.

```text
USB VBUS 5V
  |
  +-- FB1 ---------------------> FT234XD.VCC
  |                                |
  |                                +--> FT234XD.3V3OUT
  |                                      |
  |                                      +--> TS3A4741.IN1/IN2
  |
  +----------------------------> TPS6282533.VIN
                                   |
                                   +-- EN = VIN
                                   |
                                   +-- SW -- L1 --> P3V3_BUCK
                                                   |
                                                   +--> MAX40200AUK+T
                                                        VDD = P3V3_BUCK
                                                        EN  = VDD
                                                        OUT = +3.3V rail
                                                              |
                                                              +--> FT234XD.VCCIO
                                                              +--> TS3A4741.V+
                                                              +--> LED1 pull-up
                                                              +--> Leafony Bus 3.3V (CN1 F1/B1)
```

`P3V3_BUCK` is the local power rail between the TPS6282533 and MAX40200. The `+3.3V rail` is the Leafony Bus power rail after the MAX40200. If another leaf supplies the Leafony Bus 3.3 V while USB is disconnected, the MAX40200 blocks reverse current along `+3.3V rail -> P3V3_BUCK -> TPS6282533.SW/VIN -> VBUS`. The voltage drop across the MAX40200 makes the effective Leafony Bus voltage lower than the TPS6282533 output.

| State | Power | UART signals | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| USB connected, no external 3.3 V | TPS6282533 supplies 3.3 V to the Leafony Bus | TS3A4741 ON | Normal USB-UART operation |
| USB disconnected, no external 3.3 V | VBUS=0 V, P3V3_BUCK=0 V, Leafony Bus 3.3 V=0 V | TS3A4741 OFF | The board is effectively powered off |
| USB disconnected, another leaf supplies 3.3 V | External power is applied to Leafony Bus 3.3 V; MAX40200 blocks reverse current toward the buck converter/VBUS | TS3A4741 OFF | Switch control is OFF because FT234XD.3V3OUT=0 V |
| USB connected, another leaf also supplies 3.3 V | Check for conflicts between power sources | TS3A4741 ON | If simultaneous supplies are allowed, verify the system's power ORing design |

When USB is disconnected and another leaf supplies 3.3 V, voltage is applied to FT234XD.VCCIO, TS3A4741.V+, and the LED1 pull-up, which are all connected to the `+3.3V rail` after the MAX40200. FT234XD.VCC comes from VBUS and is therefore 0 V; FT234XD.3V3OUT is also 0 V. The TS3A4741 disconnects UART TX/RX.

In this state, the estimated battery current flowing into the USB-C leaf is approximately 0.15 µA typical and 2.3 µA maximum, based on datasheet specifications. This consists of MAX40200 reverse leakage (0.07 µA typical / 1.5 µA maximum) and TS3A4741 VCC standby current (0.075 µA typical / 0.75 µA maximum). FT234XD is excluded from this estimate because VCC=0 V with VCCIO=3.3 V is outside its normal operating conditions specified in the datasheet. Measure the Leafony Bus 3.3 V current on actual hardware with USB disconnected.

### Backfeed prevention

| Path | Risk | Measure |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| UART TX/RX signals | Another leaf's MCU TX/RX can partially power FT234XD through its I/O protection structures | Insert TS3A4741 in series with TX/RX and turn it OFF when USB is disconnected |
| 3.3 V power line | Another leaf's 3.3 V can flow backward from TPS6282533 SW/L1 toward VIN/VBUS | Insert MAX40200AUK+T in series between P3V3_BUCK and Leafony Bus 3.3 V |

TS3A4741 IN1/IN2 connect to FT234XD.3V3OUT. With USB connected, FT234XD operates and 3V3OUT goes High, connecting TX/RX. With USB disconnected, 3V3OUT becomes 0 V and TX/RX are physically disconnected.

MAX40200 VDD connects to `P3V3_BUCK`, OUT to Leafony Bus 3.3 V, and EN to VDD. It supplies the Leafony Bus from the TPS6282533 when USB is connected and blocks reverse current from Leafony Bus 3.3 V toward the buck converter/VBUS when USB is disconnected.

### USB Type-C configuration

The USB-C port is configured as a device (UFP/Sink).

| Signal | Connection |
| :--- | :--- |
| CC1, CC2 | Each pulled down to GND through 5.1 kΩ |
| VBUS | A4, A9, B4, and B9 tied together to the 5 V input |
| GND | A1, A12, B1, and B12 connected to the ground plane |
| D+, D- | Signals with the same name on sides A and B connected on the PCB and routed to FT234XD |
| SBU1, SBU2 | NC |

USB PD is not supported. The CC resistors alone identify the port as a USB Type-C Sink/UFP.

### ESD protection

USBLC6-2P6 protects the D+/D- lines. It is placed near the USB-C connector to keep stubs on D+/D- short. VBUS enters the board through FB1. Consider provisions for an additional VBUS TVS diode if needed.

### Communication indicator LED

FT234XD CBUS0 is configured for `TX&RXLED#` mode to drive a shared TX/RX communication indicator LED.

## Leafony Bus pin assignment

| Pin name | Front / Back | Signal | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3.3V | F1 / B1 | +3.3V rail | 3.3 V power after MAX40200; supplies up to 500 mA from USB to other leaves |
| VBUS | F3 / B3 | VBUS 5V | USB VBUS, available to other leaves that need it |
| D0 | F18 / B18 | UART TX | From FT234XD TXD to another leaf's MCU RX, through TS3A4741 Ch1 |
| D1 | F20 / B20 | UART RX | From another leaf's MCU TX to FT234XD RXD, through TS3A4741 Ch2 |
| GND | F27 / B27 | GND | Common ground |

## Main components

| Ref | Part number | Function |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| U1 | TS3A4741DCNR | 2-channel SPST analog switch for disconnecting UART TX/RX |
| U2 | USBLC6-2P6 | USB D+/D- ESD protection |
| U3 | FT234XD | USB-UART bridge |
| U4 | TPS6282533DMQR | Buck converter generating 3.3 V from 5 V |
| U5 | MAX40200AUK+T | Ideal diode preventing reverse current in the 3.3 V power line |
| J1 | CX90M-16P | USB Type-C receptacle |
| L1 | 0.47uH | Inductor for TPS6282533 |
| FB1 | 600Ω @ 100MHz | VBUS input noise suppression |

## Software

### Uploading to AP01 AVR MCU

In the [published schematic](https://github.com/leafony/az01c-usb-c/blob/main/kicad/leafony-az01c.kicad_sch), FT234XD has no DTR pin and its RTS pin is unconnected. AZ01C therefore has no connection that drives the MCU RESET signal and cannot reset AP01 simply by opening the port. The D2 in the IC pin name `RTS/D2` is an alternate IC function, not a connection to Leafony Bus D2.

1. In Arduino IDE, select **Arduino Pro or Pro Mini**, processor **ATmega328P (3.3V, 8 MHz)**, and the serial port that belongs to AZ01C.
2. Run **Verify** to check compilation. Close other IDE instances, serial monitors, or applications using the same port.
3. Hold the AP01 reset switch while starting **Upload**. Release it when the IDE switches from compiling to uploading.
4. Check that the IDE reports upload completion. If it reports `not in sync` or a similar error, check the board and port settings and try adjusting the release timing.

The time available after reset depends on the bootloader installed on AP01. Match the reset release to the start of uploading rather than relying on a fixed number of seconds.

If the LCD or another leaf covers the switch, disconnect **all power sources, including USB and batteries**, before removing that leaf. After uploading, disconnect all power again before rebuilding the stack. Unplugging USB does not power-reset the MCU while another supply remains active.

### Drivers

Use the official FTDI VCP or D2XX driver.

| OS | Driver | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Windows 10/11 | Standard driver installed automatically | Use the official FTDI driver if needed |
| macOS | Standard Apple FTDI driver | macOS 10.9 or later |
| Linux | `ftdi_sio` | Automatically recognized by many distributions |

### Initial configuration (FT_PROG)

Configure the following values in the FT234XD's built-in MTP before mass production.

| Parameter | Value | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| CBUS0 Function | `TX&RXLED#` | For the LED1 communication indicator |
| Manufacturer Name | User-defined | Example: `mitdir` |
| Product Description | User-defined | Example: `Leafony USB-UART Bridge` |
| Serial Number | Unique value | Identifies each device when multiple units are connected |
| USB Vendor ID | `0x0403` | FTDI default |
| USB Product ID | `0x6015` | FT-X default |

## Design considerations

- Verify that FT234XD can tolerate VCC=0 V with VCCIO=3.3 V when USB is disconnected and another leaf supplies 3.3 V.
- Measure the current flowing from Leafony Bus 3.3 V into the USB-C leaf on actual hardware with USB disconnected and another leaf supplying 3.3 V.
- If another leaf's 3.3 V supply is also active while USB is connected, check for conflicts between power sources and verify the power ORing design.
- Account for the MAX40200 voltage drop and verify that the minimum voltage on the Leafony Bus 3.3 V rail meets the requirements of the connected leaves.

# AZ02 RTC&microSD

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az02/

## Features

Read the date and time, and save or read data on a microSD card with this leaf. It includes an NXP PCF8523TK real-time clock (RTC) and a microSD card slot. The RTC can also send alarm and timer interrupts to the [MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu). The RTC uses [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c), and the microSD card uses [SPI](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#spi).

# AZ61 Connector

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/others/az61/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/others/az61/az61a_large.jpg)

## Features

Connect signal and power lines between stacked leaves with this connector. The Leafony Platform uses ACR (Anisotropic Conductive Rubber): conductive elements arranged at a narrow pitch within insulating silicone rubber. Compressing the connector between leaves creates the electrical connections.

# Power

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/

Choose a leaf to view its specifications, pin assignments and technical documents.

- [AV01 CR2032](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av01/): Supply 3.3V power from a CR2032 coin cell battery.
- [AV02 CR2450](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av02/): Supply 3.3V power from a CR2450 coin cell battery.
- [AV03 AA BAT](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av03/): Supply 3.3V power from a single AA battery.
- [AV04A 2V～4.5V](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av04/): Supply 3.3V power from an external battery through a JST SH connector.
- [AV06 1.8V–5.5V](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av06/): Supply 3.3V power at up to 1.0A from an external battery through a JST PH connector, and read the battery voltage from an MCU leaf.

See also the [leaf reference index](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/) and [I²C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/).

# AV01 CR2032

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/power/av01/

[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/power/av01/av01a_f_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/power/av01/av01a_b_large.jpg)
[](https://docs.leafony.com/leaf/power/av01/av01a_p_large.jpg)

## Features

Supply 3.3V power to the leaves from a CR2032 coin cell battery. You can turn the power on or off with the switch and read the battery voltage from an [MCU (microcontroller)](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#mcu) leaf.

This leaf includes a CR2032 battery holder, a step-up power supply circuit that converts the battery's 3V to 3.3V, and an [I2C](https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/#i2c)-connected AD converter for measuring battery voltage.

## Specification
