# Which programming languages can I use with STM32?

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/stm32-language/

Leafony AP03 development is intended to use C/C++ with Arduino IDE or STM32CubeIDE. Arduino sketches are based on C++.

**You can write programs in C and C++.** Leafony's [AP03 STM32 MCU](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/processor/ap03/) is intended for **development with Arduino IDE or STM32CubeIDE**.

An Arduino program is called a "sketch." A sketch in an `.ino` file is compiled as a **C++-based program**. Knowledge of variables, conditions, loops, and functions learned in C is useful here too.

- `setup()`: Runs once at startup. Use it to initialize sensors, communication, and other settings.
- `loop()`: Runs repeatedly afterward. Use it for tasks such as reading sensors and sending data.

If you are new to this, set up the [development environment](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/) and [libraries and board definitions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/libraries/), then choose an STM32 example from the [sample catalog](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/). Start by changing small parts of its values or behavior.

ST's [STM32CubeIDE](https://www.st.com/en/development-tools/stm32cubeide.html) supports C/C++ development and debugging with a debugger. See [connecting a debugger](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/stm32_debug/) for the AP03 connection setup. An Arduino sketch cannot simply be opened as a CubeIDE project, so start with the environment specified by a Leafony Arduino sample when trying that sample.

Reference: [Arduino's sketch build process](https://docs.arduino.cc/arduino-cli/sketch-build-process/)

---

# How should I match the STM32 Core and RTC library versions?

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/stm32-rtc-core/

STM32RTC and the Arduino Core require compatible versions. Check current requirements when using an older sample too.

Choose **compatible versions of STM32RTC and the STM32 Arduino Core** supplied by your board configuration. The current Docs also explains [library versions in older samples](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/#library-versions-in-older-samples).

If an older sample produces a compatibility error such as `Please update the core`, compare the settings below. Check whether the Core meets the library’s requirements.

- **Arduino IDE:** Check the selected package and version in Boards Manager, and the STM32RTC version in Library Manager. Distinguish the Leafony package for AP03 from the generic STM32 package.
- **PlatformIO:** Check `framework-arduinoststm32` in the build log and `lib_deps` in `platformio.ini`.

The current [STM32RTC requirements](https://github.com/stm32duino/STM32RTC#requirement) specify library 1.x for Core 1.3.0 or later, below 3.x, and library 2.x for Core 3.x or later. Earlier 1.x releases may have different requirements, so also check the README and header for the version you use. If you use STM32LowPower, match [its requirements](https://github.com/stm32duino/STM32LowPower#requirement) too.

See [Libraries and board definitions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/libraries/) and [PlatformIO setup](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/) for AP03 settings. Keep a copy of your original configuration and try building a small sample before returning to your program.

**Historical question consulted:** [“leafony の STM32 Simple BLE Beacon について” by tiri-leafony-users](https://ja.stackoverflow.com/questions/96470/) (October 11, 2023, Japanese). This answer summarizes version-selection guidance that remains useful today; it does not imply that the original error is still occurring.

---

# STM32 program does not run after “upload complete”

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/stm32-upload-run/

Check the AP03 Program/Run switch, reset sequence, and upload verification log. The completion message alone can be misleading.

On AP03, **change the switch position between programming and running, and reset after each change.** Check this sequence:

1. Close the serial monitor and other apps using the same port.
2. Set AP03 to **Program**, reset it, and upload.
3. Check that connection, programming, and verification succeeded in the programmer’s log.
4. Set the switch back to **Run** and reset again to start the program.

Arduino IDE may show a completion message while the log contains `Timeout error occured while waiting for acknowledgement`. In PlatformIO, check the STM32CubeProgrammer verification result as well as `SUCCESS`.

See the [Arduino IDE instructions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/arduino_ide/) or [PlatformIO instructions](https://docs.leafony.com/en/environment/stm32/platformio/) for switch locations and log examples. If only serial output is missing, check that the monitor’s port and baud rate match your program’s `Serial.begin()` setting.

These steps apply to AP03. For another MCU, use that model’s upload instructions.

Buy kits and leaves from Leafony Shop. Each product page has current prices, stock, and lead times.

You can buy kits and leaves from [Leafony Shop](https://shop.leafony.com/).

If you are getting started, the [kits and products page](https://docs.leafony.com/en/products/) helps you compare kit contents before visiting the shop product pages.

Each product page has current pricing, stock, and lead-time information. Some products with documentation may be discontinued or awaiting release.

For a standard purchase, choose products and quantities on the product pages, then proceed from the cart to checkout. To choose a configuration, check [Combining leaves and choosing power](https://docs.leafony.com/en/guides/combining-leaves/) and the [example catalog](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/).

If you need an individual quotation document, use the [Leafony Shop contact page (Japanese)](https://shop.leafony.com/pages/contact-us).

# Can a Windows C# app receive Leafony BLE data?

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/windows-ble/

With a configuration that supports GATT communication, you can build a receiver using Windows BLE APIs. Start by checking UUIDs and the data format.

Yes. **If your configuration runs a BLE sample that uses GATT communication, you can build a receiver using Windows BLE APIs.** Match the PC receiver to the program running on Leafony.

Start with the [AVR Web Bluetooth sample](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/avr-mcu/basic/webbluetooth_iot/) or [STM32 sample](https://docs.leafony.com/en/examples/advanced/stm32-mcu/stm32/stm32_webbluetooth_iot/) and its receiver code.

1. Identify the leaves and the program running on them.
2. Check service and characteristic UUIDs and how Read, Write, and Notify are used.
3. Discover the service on Windows and implement the appropriate operations, such as subscribing to notifications.
4. Interpret the received bytes using the same format as the sample.

[Microsoft’s GATT client guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/apps/develop/devices-sensors/gatt-client) includes C# examples for service discovery and notifications. A device name alone does not explain its data, so also check [the BLE data format](https://docs.leafony.com/en/questions/ble-data-format/).

Also check support for your Windows SDK, app type, adapter, and driver. A beacon-only sample behaves differently from connection-based GATT communication.

**Historical question consulted:** [“leafonyの開発環境について教えてください” by ike](https://ja.stackoverflow.com/questions/99110/) (April 15, 2024, Japanese). This answer does not recommend that older environment; it describes how to build a receiver using current official documentation.

# Terms

URL: https://docs.leafony.com/en/terms/

Understand terms used in Leafony documentation: BLE, I2C, SPI and UART communication; MCU, MEMS and PWM; leaves, the Leafony bus and related organizations.

*Alphabetical order*

## BLE

Bluetooth Low Energy is a wireless communication technology designed for low-power data transfer. Leafony uses it, for example, to send sensor readings to a compatible smartphone or computer. Both the device and the application need to support the connection. See the [Bluetooth SIG technology overview](https://www.bluetooth.com/learn-about-bluetooth/tech-overview/) for more information.

## DC

DC stands for Direct Current, in which current flows in one direction. A DC motor operates from a DC power supply. The [AIx1 Motor leaf](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/aix1/) uses a motor supply and a motor driver to control motors in response to MCU signals.

## I2C

I2C stands for Inter-Integrated Circuit and is pronounced "I-squared-C" or "I-two-C." It is a communication interface that connects a microcontroller to sensors and other devices. Devices share two signal lines, SDA for data and SCL for timing, and addresses identify the communication partner. Power and ground connections are also required. See the [I2C address map](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/i2c-address-map/) for Leafony addresses and the [NXP I2C-bus specification](https://www.nxp.com/docs/en/user-guide/UM10204.pdf) for details.

## IoT/CPS

IoT stands for Internet of Things and CPS stands for Cyber-Physical Systems. CPS refers to systems that connect physical and digital spaces.

## Jumper pin

A small part placed over adjacent pins to connect them electrically, also called a shunt or shorting jumper. It is often used to change a board setting. It is different from a jumper wire, which connects terminals using a wire.

## Jumper wire

A wire used to connect terminals, often for prototyping with breadboards or pin headers. Male ends plug into sockets, while female ends fit over pins. Choose the combination that matches the terminals you are connecting.

## LCD

LCD stands for Liquid Crystal Display, a type of screen used to display text, numbers, or images. Leafony's [AI04 LCD](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai04/) is a character display with two rows of eight characters.

## Leaf

A leaf is an electronic board or module, typically about 2 cm square, that forms the basis of Leafony. It is called a leaf because it is small and green. More precisely, a leaf is an electronic board that has a Leafony bus. You can easily create your own original leaves and sell them commercially by labeling them "Leafony compliant."

## Leafony or the Leafony platform

Leafony is an open hardware and software platform built by combining leaves. Its very small size and low power consumption make it suitable for prototyping IoT/CPS systems and improving development efficiency. Leafony also works in the Arduino environment, so you can use the many software resources available online. You can also develop software in environments other than Arduino.

Leafony is a word coined from Leaf and Symphony. It expresses the hope that individual leaves will come together to create new value, just as the sounds of different instruments combine to make music.

Leafony technical information is generally free to use, including for commercial purposes. See the License section for details. Companies and individuals sell their own leaves labeled "Leafony compliant," and such activities are encouraged. However, Leafony is a registered trademark, so please refrain from including Leafony in product names to avoid market confusion.

## Leafony block

It is an electronic device that is made up of multiple leaves. Normally, stacked leaves form a block, so it is called a leaf block. An electronic device made by combining leaves, even if the structure is flat and spread out, is called a leaf block.

## Leafony bus

A common pathway that connects multiple leaves to each other is called a Leafony bus. Its electrical and physical specifications define the signal and power connections. It typically occupies a 20 mm x 5.5 mm area on a leaf. A Leafony bus-compliant leaf can communicate with other leaves, but whether it works with the Leafony platform without problems also depends on the software and other factors. Leafony bus compliance therefore indicates connectivity close to the physical level.

The Leafony bus artwork is copyrighted and published under the CC-BY License. You may use it free of charge, including commercially, by stating "Leafony compliant." You are therefore free to develop and sell your own leaves. However, Leafony is a registered trademark, so do not label the leaves you make with Leafony itself. A leaf bearing the Leafony label indicates that its product quality has been verified.

## Leafony connector

A connector newly developed to interconnect leaves using anisotropic conductive rubber. It serves as both a male and female connector. Leaves can also be connected using techniques such as solder-based thermocompression bonding, but using a Leafony connector is simpler.

## LEAFONY SYSTEMS Co., Ltd.

LEAFONY SYSTEMS was the company that manufactured and sold Leafony products with the registered Leafony trademark, based on the research and development by the Trillion Node Engine Project. Leaves bearing the Leafony label had their interoperability verified by the project.

In March 2026, LEAFONY SYSTEMS transferred its entire business to MITDIR Inc.

## MITDIR Inc.

MITDIR Inc. acquired the entire business of LEAFONY SYSTEMS Co., Ltd. in March 2026 and currently handles the sales and support of Leafony products. By combining Leafony with its existing IoT and AI technologies, MITDIR works to provide DX solutions and promote IoT technology through collaboration with the research community.

Leafony bus-compliant leaves are also sold by other companies and individuals under the "Leafony compliant" label, and such activities are encouraged. However, Leafony is not included in those product names.

## MCU

MCU stands for Microcontroller Unit. It is an IC that runs programs to read sensors and control outputs such as LEDs or motors. It includes a CPU, memory, and input/output functions. A Leafony board carrying an MCU is called an MCU leaf.

## MEMS

MEMS stands for Micro-Electro-Mechanical Systems. The term refers to technology and devices that use tiny mechanical structures and electronic circuits. A MEMS microphone converts the movement of a tiny membrane caused by sound into an electrical signal. [AI03 MIC&VR&LED](https://docs.leafony.com/en/leaf/io/ai03/) includes a MEMS microphone.

## PWM

PWM stands for Pulse Width Modulation. A signal switches on and off at a regular interval, while the proportion of time spent on is varied. It can be used to adjust LED brightness or motor output through a motor driver. The proportion of on-time is called the duty cycle.

## SPI

SPI stands for Serial Peripheral Interface. It transfers data between a microcontroller and peripheral devices in time with a clock signal. Leafony uses SPI for devices such as microSD cards. Check each leaf's specifications for the signals used to select a device and the pin assignments.

## Trillion-node engine

The electronics platform developed by the Trillion Node Engine Project. Hardware and software whose research and development has been completed are organized and released to the public under the name Leafony.

## Trillion-node engine project

The Trillion Node Engine Project is a research and development project commissioned and subsidized by the New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO).

## Trillion-node study-group

Many IT nodes, including IoT/CPS systems, are expected to be used throughout society in the future. The Trillion-node study-group discusses that future and shares information. It uses Leafony as a practical basis for these discussions and works to promote its use to support the development of IoT/CPS. It also provides a place to connect related companies with needs and technologies to offer.

## UART

UART stands for Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter. It provides serial communication using TX to transmit and RX to receive data. Both devices need matching settings such as the communication speed. Leafony uses UART between MCU and communication leaves, and for communication with a computer through a USB-to-UART leaf.

## Harness

Electrical connections between a Leafony block and the outside world may require wiring. Such wiring is called a harness.
